A small piece of heaven for a family broken by tragedy. In July, Sierra Sharry and Lane Smith were about to welcome their baby. Sharry was eight months pregnant. Then Lane fell and hit his head. He was taken to OU Medical Center in Oklahoma City, but he never woke up. "July 13th, 2014 was the worst day of my life," Sharry wrote on Facebook. "I lost my best friend. The father of my unborn child." Their son, Taos, was born a few weeks later. When Taos was six months old, Sharry asked the photographer to help make their family feel whole, just for one picture.

You probably already have an opinion about Indiana's religious freedom law. Some people support the growing number of companies that criticize the law, saying it lets businesses turn away gay and lesbian people by claiming religion. Others, like Indiana Governor Mike Pence, are surprised by the anger. They say the law is similar to one already used at the federal level and in 19 other states. The debate is strong because religious freedom and gay rights often clash. Also, people question how the law is written and what the real reasons behind it are.

Some fans of Lucille Ball want her statue removed from a park in her hometown, Celoron, New York. They say the statue looks unflattering and doesn't match her famous image as the star of "I Love Lucy." The life-size bronze statue has been compared to singer Conway Twitty, the snake from "Beetlejuice," and actor Steve Buscemi— all unflattering looks. Even the local mayor, Scott Schrecengost, has said he doesn't like the statue. It shows Lucille Ball holding a bottle of the fake drink Vitameatavegamin from her show. But despite the criticism, the statue has been popular with tourists since 20009. It draws visitors who come to Celoron to take pictures with it.

The last time Muhammadu Buhari became president of Nigeria, he took power by force. This time, he won through a fair election. Here are five reasons why this election, one of the most heated in Nigeria’s history, matters so much. For the first time ever, the opposition party beat the ruling party in a democratic election. Muhammadu Buhari, who is 77 (likely meaning 72), won the presidential election, beating the current president, Goodluck Jonathan, by about two million votes. Nigeria is important because it has the largest economy and the most people in Africa. It is also one of Africa’s top oil producers and sends a lot of crude oil to the United States.

People in Iran were extremely excited, almost like they had won a big international game. But what happened was even more important. After a major nuclear agreement with the U States and other countries, Iran is expected to end years of strict international sanctions and isolation. The deal was announced just before midnight on Thursday. In Tehran, on Vali Asr Street, one of the city’s main roads, people celebrated like it was a festival. Cars honked their horns, people danced in the middle of traffic, and some even showed off U.S. dollar bills. Young people waved flags from their car roofs, played loud music, and shared their joy online using the hashtag #IranTalks.

A fourth man, Dilkhayot Kasimov, has been charged in a Brooklyn federal court indictment related to a plan to help terrorists and possibly join ISIS. The indictment says he is accused of helping provide support to terrorists. The three other men already charged—Abdurasul Hasanovich Juraboev, Akhror Saidakhmetov, and Abror Habibov—were charged with two counts of supporting a foreign terrorist group. They have all said not guilty. It is not known if Kasimov has been arrested.

CNN reported that the third blood moon in a four-part series was the shortest eclipse of the group. However, it still offered a beautiful sight for early morning viewers in North America. The moon completely entered Earth's shadow at 4:58 a.m. Pacific Time (7:58 a.m. Eastern Time) on Saturday. This total lunar eclipse lasted about five minutes — the shortest total eclipse of the century, according to NASA. Before, during, and after the total eclipse, the moon had a burnt-orange color, which is why total lunar eclipses are called "blood moons."

Istanbul, Turkey (CNN)  
On Tuesday, many Turks were scared and confused. An older woman wearing a white headscarf and carrying shopping bags stood outside a busy subway station, asking, "What's happening? Why can't I get in?" She was one of millions affected by the worst power outage in Turkey in over ten years. Dozens of cities lost electricity for several hours. Millions of people were impacted, including passengers stuck on stopped trains and subtrays.

During this Holy Week, let’s remember what God’s word says about fair wages and fair treatment. Isaiah 58.6 says: "This is the kind of fast I want: to break the chains of injustice, remove exploitation at work, free the oppressed, and cancel debts." The McDonald's decision to raise wages for 90,000 employees is a big win for fast-food cooks and cashiers, and for all of us who support them. Workers are making it harder for successful companies like McDonald's to pay wages so low that workers can't escape poverty. by standing together.

California may soon be known for the color of its lawns—brown. Governor Jerry Brown has ordered the first mandatory water cuts for residents, businesses, and farms. Cities and towns across the drought-straffected state must cut water use by 25%. Brown said this marks a new era, and that picture of a green lawn getting water every day is over. The 25% reduction means about 1.5 million acre-feet of water will be saved over the next nine months. The state says one acre-foot of water is about 325,000 gallons.

London (CNN) – Voters in the UK have little time left to decide who they want to support, as polling stations open across the country in a general election that could shift the political scene. The campaign has been very short, especially compared to the long U States elections. The result could be a change in government, with David Cameron’s Conservative Party possibly losing power to the Labour Party, led by Ed Miliband. Or it could lead to a complicated process where party leaders try to form deals with smaller parties. But we won’t know the outcome until after the polls close late Thursday evening, local time.

This time of year, Christians around the world—over 2 billion people—think about Jesus’ death and resurrection. But this Holy Week, because of the deadly attack on Christian students in Kenya and the continuing danger faced by Christians in other countries, we are asking Christians to also remember how many Christians and others have been cruced, beheaded, stoned, forced into slavery, sexually abused, trafficked, harassed, bombed, or driven from their homes—just because they follow their faith.

Three Ferguson, Missouri, city employees — including a police captain and a sergeant — were forced to resign or were fired after racist and offensive emails they sent were made public. The emails were found during a U.S. Justice Department investigation into racism in Ferguson’s police and court systems. The messages contained hateful remarks about President Barack Obama, First Lady Michelle Obama, Muslims, and other minorities. The Washington Post obtained the emails through a public records request on Thursday. CNN looked at the emails on Friday. The employees involved were Police Captain Rick Henke and Sergeant.

Two people, including a licensed greyhound trainer, have been arrested in Australia after at least 55 dog bodies were found dumped in the bush in Queensland. The two suspects are from Bundaberg — a 71-year-old man and a 64-year-old woman. Each was charged with illegally having a firearm, according to ABC news. The woman, who is a licensed greyhound trainer, was also charged with blocking police. Michael Beatty, a spokesperson for RSPCA Queensland, said the investigation is still ongoing. RSPCA Queensland is helping the police with their investigation.

Two years ago, Mike Premeau and Kathy Danke started a small business called Memories Gourmet Pizza Co. in their Wisconsin town. They sold frozen pizzas, including breakfast and gluten-free ones, in stores across Nichols, which is west of Green Bay. They built a loyal customer base. But this week, their business was at risk because some people confused them with Memories Pizza in Walkerton, Indiana. That other pizza place made national news when its owners said they would refuse to cater a same-sex wedding. Angry people posted comments on Memories Gourmet Pizza's Facebook page and called their phone to protest.

Archaeologists in Austria found the complete skeleton of a camel under a cellar. The discovery was made between 2006 and 2007 during a dig for a shopping center in the town of Tulln. The team was from the University of Veterinary Medicine Vienna (Vetmeduni). At first, they thought it might be a large horse or cow. But after looking at the neck bones, lower jaw, and forearm bones, expert Alfred Galik said it was clearly a camel. This camel may have been used by Ottoman soldiers during their 17th-century siege of Vienna.

Andrew Getty, the 4-year-old grandson of J. Paul Getty, died Tuesday afternoon at his home in Los Angeles. His parents, Ann and Gordon Getty, made the announcement in a statement. They asked the media and the public to respect their privacy during this hard time. The Los Angeles County coroner's office said Getty's death "appears to be from natural causes or an accident." An assistant coroner, Ed Winter, told CNN's KTLA affiliate that some medication was found at Getty's home. But it's unclear if he was taking it or what his medical history was.

We may never fully understand why co-pilot Andreas Lubitz crashed Germanwings Flight 9424 into the French Alps on March 2. The latest report shows he increased the plane’s speed during its descent. This is a terrible event. As the investigation continues, we will learn more about how much Lubitz hid his mental illness, whether he asked for help, and how his depression affected his ability to fly. Should he have stopped working? Should his doctors have warned someone? His case brings up serious questions about people with mental illness and the shame and fear that often come with it.

A flu outbreak has been found in Chicago, but it only affects animals, not people. A new tunnel is planned to connect Denmark and Germany under the sea, with roads and train tracks. On this page, you can read today’s full show transcript and sign up to be on the CNN Student News Roll Call.

(CNN) He didn't give his real name. But the name "Gertrude" tattooed on his neck gave him away. That's what Kankakee County, Illinois, Sheriff Tim Bukowski said on Saturday about Kamron Taylor, a 23-year-old man who was convicted of murder and later escaped from jail. Taylor was arrested overnight in Chicago. Authorities had been searching for him since early Wednesday, when he attacked a correctional officer at the Kankakee County jail, took the officer's uniform and car, and then fled. The last time officials saw Taylor was on surveillance video, just before midnight Friday, in Chicago. "They saw a man who matched the description," Bukowski said.

As his military career comes to an end, Prince Harry is going to Australia. He is 30 and will arrive on Monday for a four-week stay with the Australian Army. He will work and live with soldiers in regiments in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth. This is not his first time with Australian troops—he has already served with them several times during his 10-year military career, a military spokesman said.

Two Florida prison guards and a former trainee have been charged with planning to kill a former inmate who was about to be released. The Florida Attorney General's office announced the charges on Thursday. The men were part of a plot that involved a KKK group called the Traditional American Knights of the Ku Kl Kl Klan. An FBI informant who was undercover in the group told police what the men said. Thomas Jordan Driver, 25, told the informant he had a fight with the former inmate and that he and David Elliot Moran, 37, wanted the man dead. Court documents show Driver said he and Moran wanted the man "six feet under," meaning they wanted him buried. Charles Thomas Newcomb, 27, was also charged.

Lausanne, Switzerland (CNN) – A group of world powers, called the P5+, reached a framework deal with Iran on its nuclear program on Thursday. The deal's success is still uncertain. The countries have until the end of June to finalize the details and write the full agreement. Still, the talks were a major step, especially for the long-stf relationship between the U.S. and Iran. The negotiations were not flashy, but they showed diplomacy at its best – effective, but also very fast-paced and intense.

An improvised bomb exploded near a U.N. vehicle traveling near Garowe, a city in northeastern Somalia, on Monday morning. Six people were killed, including four aid workers from UNICEF. Somalia’s president said the attack was "an attack against the future of our country." This happened after another incident on Sunday, when three African Union troops were killed in an ambush in the Lower Shabelle region of Somalia.. The terrorist group Al-Shabaab said it carried out Monday’s attack. The explosion happened around 8 a.m. in the administrative capital of the autonomous Puntland region, according to the United Nations Assistance Mission in Somalia.

Prince Harry arrived in Australia on Monday. He is 30 years old. Before starting his military duties, he visited the Australian War Memorial in Canberra, the capital city. He paid his respects at the Tomb of the Unknown Australian Soldier. A crowd gathered outside the memorial. Some people took photos of him, and one boy held a sign that said, "Red Heads Rule!" during his four-week stay in Australia, Harry will live and work with members of the Australian Army in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth, according to the Australian Defence Forces.

Australia, a key ally of the United States, has agreed to share some of its intelligence with Iran. Australian Foreign Minister Julie Bishop said the agreement is informal and mainly focuses on monitoring Australians who travel to Iraq to fight with ISIS. One Australian politician called the move "dancing with the devil." Bishop became the first Australian government minister to visit Iran in two years. She met with Iranian President Hassan Rouhani over the weekend. The intelligence deal was announced in an interview Bishop gave to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation while she was in Tehran.

Marseille, France (CNN) – Initial tests on the flight data recorder from Germanwings Flight 9525 show that co-pilot Andreas Lubitz intentionallyy made the plane dive faster, according to the French air accident investigation agency, the BEA. The flight data recorder, also called the "black box," was found on Thursday by search teams who had been looking for it in the mountains of the French Alps since the crash on March 24. A statement from the BEA on Friday said they started examining the recorder's data right away.

CNN reported that a 110-day chase from Antarctic waters to west Africa ended unexpectedly when the crew of a suspected illegal fishing vessel, the Thunder, were rescued by conservation group Sea Shepherd. The Thunder had been wanted by Interpol under a "purple notice" for suspected fraud and fishing crimes. Sea Shepherd had been tracking the Thunder since their ship, the Bob Barker, first spotted it in the Southern Ocean months earlier. The chase ended early Monday in the Gulf of Guinea, off west Africa, when the Bob Barker received a distress call from the Thunder.

Most days, 16-year-old Jason Zobott arrives at Huntley High School, a high school in the suburbs of Chicago, around 7:30 a.m., just like other high school students. But what he does after that is different. Jason is in Huntley High’s blended learning program, which combines online learning with regular classroom teaching. One-third of the school’s 2,700 students are in the program. The school wants most of its students to join by 2015. Jason, who is a top student in his grade and also takes part in many after-school activities, says he likes the online part because it lets him do his schoolwork anytime and learn at his own pace.

Garissa, Kenya (CNN) – After a deadly Al-Shabaab attack on Kenyan soil, Kenya conducted airstrikes against the group in Somalia. A military source said the strikes were not punishment for the recent massacre at Garissa University College, which killed almost 50 people. The source said the airstrikes were part of a long-term military operation that began in 2011 and are not connected to the Garissa attack. The military source spoke on Monday but chose not to give their name, which is common practice for Kenyan military officials.

Pope Francis reminded the world that the Vatican is a country and that he serves as a moral leader during his usual Easter message. He spoke about the pain people are facing in ongoing wars, especially in Iraq and Syria. He called for an end to violence in those places and said that help must reach those who are suffering. He urged the global community not to ignore the serious humanitarian crisis in these countries or the struggles of the many refugees. He made this message in his "urbi et orbi" speech, which means "to the city (Rome) and to the world."

CNN reported that Duke University students and faculty marched Wednesday afternoon, shouting "We are not afraid. We stand together," after a noose was found hanging from a tree on campus. Duke officials asked anyone with information about the noose—which was discovered near a student center at 2 a.m.—to contact campus police. A photo of the noose spread quickly on social media, causing anger in the community. Later, hundreds of people gathered at a forum on the steps of Duke Chapel, close to where the noose was found. One speaker said, "You came here for the reason that you want to say with me, 'This is no Duke we will accept. This is no Duke we want. This is not the Duke we're here to experience."

A U.S. citizen, Muhanad Mahmoud Al Farekh, 29, did not enter a plea during his first court hearing on Thursday. He was deported from Pakistan to the U.S. He is accused of planning to fight against U.S. forces overseas. The charges are based on a complaint filed in U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York in Brooklyn. CNN counterterrorism analyst Philip Mudd said the case is "news for celebration."

A Saudi border guard was killed in a fight with militants along the border between Saudi Arabia and Yemen this week, according to the Saudi Press Agency (SPA). This is the first time since Saudi Arabia began its airstrikes in Yemen that a Saudi military death has been officially reported.

. The clash happened Wednesday night in the Asir region in southwestern Saudi Arabia. Militants in a mountainous area of Yemen fired on Saudi border troops, who then fired back. The dead guard was identified as Corporal Salman Ali Yahya al-Maliki. Ten other people were injured, but the injuries were not serious.

Dubai (CNN) I felt a little nervous starting the Al Marmoum camel race in Dubai. As the only Gulf national on the CNN team, people expected me to know about camel racing — a long-standing tradition here. But even though I tried wearing a kandora, the UAE national dress, my modern way of life makes me feel like a stranger in this world. A friendly farm owner took us into the majlis — a special meeting area — where camel owners were gathering. The room was big and beautifully decorated, like a fancy theater. The camel owners were sitting on the floor, eating a traditional Arabic meal of fish and rice, called a'aish. The room was full of loud, excited talk.

Havana, Cuba — Charlie Hill is sitting in a dark bar on a very sunny day in Havana. "Hey man," he says, his voice rough from smoking, nodding like he knows you’ve been looking for him. But a lot of people have been looking for Charlie Hill for a long time. For 43 years, Cuba has given him shelter from charges that he killed a New Mexico police officer and hijacked an airplane to Havana. Hill is now 65. He agreed to talk to CNN after we spent two years trying to find him. He says he’s now thinking about leaving Cuba and going back to the United States.

Misao Okawa, who was listed in Guinness World Records as the oldest person in the world, has died at the age of 117. She passed away on Wednesday morning in Osaka, Japan, according to Tadahi Uchimura, a local official. Okawa had three children, four grandchildren, and six great grandchildren. She was born on March 5, 1898. Her family owned a kimono shop in Osaka. Satoshi Yoshioka, an employee at the nursing home where she lived since 1997, said she was a quiet, kind person who loved to eat. Her favorite foods were sushi and udon noodles. She had eaten a lot of cake for her birthday in March 2000000o0o

Washington (CNN) – When the Missouri National Guard was sent to Ferguson, Missouri, to help deal with riots that happened off and on last year, they used strong military language like "enemy forces" and "adversaries" to describe the protesters. Documents obtained by CNN show this. The guard went to help local police, who many community leaders and civil rights groups said used too much force and made the tense situation worse during protests that happened occasionally from August until the end of the year..

Mogadishu, Somalia (CNN) – Gunmen attacked the headquarters of Somalia's education ministry in the capital on Tuesday. The attack started with a suicide car bomb that exploded at the entrance of the two-story building. The Ministry of Education, Culture & Higher Education is located there. After the blast, five gunmen entered the building and opened fire, killing at least 12 people and injuring 16 others, officials said. The Islamist militant group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for the attack. Their spokesman, Abu Musab, said they carried it out. The Somali National Security Ministry spokesman, Mohamed Yusuf, confirmed the details of the attack.

Gregory Margolin is now 87 years old. When he was 16, he joined the Soviet Red Army and fought against the Nazis in World War II. At the time, he was a Jewish soldier, but he didn't tell others. He says, "I didn’t show I was Jewish, but it didn’t matter—people were dying all around me." This year, he found himself back in a war zone in Ukraine. He had once been a sniper and later became a commander in the army. His old military uniform still has the medals he earned during the war. His granddaughter, Liora, still listens to his war stories with amazement. She can't believe he lived through it all.

More than 200 Nigerian schoolgirls vanished. It happened in Chibok, in northeastern Nigeria, during the night, while they were in their school dorms. It has now been 365 days since they were taken. They are still missing. This is a terrible thing, and we should all feel ashamed. We should be ashamed that in our world, violent extremists can take young girls without being punished. We should also feel ashamed that people quickly stop paying attention to such tragedies, even when innocent lives are at stake.

CNN. Video may have killed the radio star, but in Norway, it's digital that's replacing FM radio. In two years, Norway will be the first country in the world to completely stop using FM radio. That doesn't mean people will lose all radio—they’ll just switch to digital radio. In Oslo, officials say many people in this country of 5 million have already made the switch................. On FM, Norwegians can only see five stations. On digital radio, there are four times as many. Half the country already listens to digital radio, said Culture Minister Thorhild Widvey.

CNN says everyone loves a good comeback story — especially one that's as big as a dinosaur. For over 10000 years, scientists thought the Brontosaurus wasn't a real, separate dinosaur. But now, a new study says it should be recognized as its own type of dinosaur. In 1879, O.C. Marsh named the Brontosaurus after finding 25 crates of bones at Como Bluff, Wyoming, according to the Yale Peabody Museum of Natural History. The dinosaur was similar to, but smaller than, the Apatosaurus, which had been discovered a few years earlier. Marsh gave it the name "Brontosaurus," which means " thunder lizard."

Al Qaeda in Yemen, which is also known as AQAP, has a new reward. They are offering 20 kilograms of gold to anyone who kills or captures two Shia Muslim leaders. These leaders are:  
  
  
  
  
  
The two leaders are:  
- Abdelmalik Bedrudin Al-Houthi, the Houthi rebel leader  
- Ali Abdullah Saleh, the former president of Yemen  
  
The reward is worth about $774,000 in value.  
  
AQAP said in a news release and a poster online that these two men are "the two heads of evil."

Before landing his gyrocopter on the Capitol lawn on Wednesday, Doug Hughes, a 61-year-old Florida postal worker, posted his plans and reasons on a website called thedemocracyclub.org. He said the flight was meant to draw attention to corruption in Washington, D.C., and to show ways to fix the system. He also said he wasn’t hiding his plan. Before flying, he emailed info@barackobama.com to tell officials he wasn’t a threat. He wanted them to know that shooting him down would cause more problems than just letting him deliver his letters to Congress.

The bad news for Rio de Janeiro keeps growing. After many dead fish were found in the Rodrigo de Freitas lagoon, officials from Rio's legislative assembly started an investigation on Monday. They want to find out why the fish died. The investigation will look at other lakes and bays in the state where similar problems have happened. The group will work with the State Environmental Institute (INEA) and the State Secretariat for the Environment. The Olympics are less than a year away, and Rio is set to host rowing and canoe events there.

Anthony Ray Hinton is 58 years old. But in many ways, he is just starting to experience life like most people do. Simple things, like using a fork, going out at night, or going to bed without someone watching over you — these are all new and strange for him. That’s because Hinton spent almost 30 years on Alabama’s death row. Just a week ago, his murder convictions were overturned, and he finally left the county jail in Birmingham. "I have to pinch myself to believe I’m really free," he told CNN’s Brooke Baldwin. "It will take time, but I’ll get used to it." Hinton had to get used to much worse. The opinion polls after the UK election debate showed no clear winner. The seven party leaders were David Cameron (Conservatives, Ed Miliband (Labour, Nick Clegg (Liberal Democrats, Nigel Farage (UKIP), Natalie Bennett (Green Party), Nicola Sturgeon (SNP), and Leanne Wood (Plaid Cymru). Comres, which was commissioned by ITV to organise the debate, found Cameron, Miliband, and Farage all tied for first with 21% each, and Sturgeon close behind with 20%. ICM, which did the poll for The Guardian, had Miliband with 25, Cameron with 24, Farage with 19, and Sturgeon with 17.

CNN reports that Facebook might soon include "Just got served divorce papers" as a relationship status. A New York judge has ruled that sending divorce papers through Facebook is a valid way to serve them. This comes after a Brooklyn woman, Ellanora Arthur Baidoo, tried for years to divorce her husband, Victor Sena Blood-Dzraku. Her lawyer, Andrew Spinnell, said they couldn’t find Mr. Blood-Dzraku to serve him with papers. Baidoo has called him several times, but he told her he has no fixed address and no job. Court documents confirm this.

It sounds like a scene from a sci-fi movie. Someone has a terrible accident and is left brain dead, on life support. Doctors talk to the family about donating organs, but instead of saving up to eight people, they’re asked to donate the whole body to save just one person—maybe someone who is paralyzed but still has a sharp mind. This may sound impossible, but Italian doctor Sergio Canavero says we’re getting close to making it real. He calls this plan HEAVEN, which stands for Head Anastomosis Venture. "Anastomosis" means to surgically connect parts together.

Anthony Stokes was supposed to have a happy ending after getting a heart transplant. Instead, on Tuesday, police said he carjied someone, broke into a house, shot at an older woman, led police on a high-speed chase, and died when his car hit a pole. In 2013, his family said an Atlanta hospital turned him down for a heart transplant. The hospital said in a letter that Stokes had a history of not following medical advice. At the time, Mark Bell was speaking for the Stokes family.

The sun had not risen at Garissa University College. Most students were still asleep in their beds. A few had gotten up for early morning Christian prayers. Then the attack started. There was an explosion and gunshots around 5:30 a.m. on Thursday (10:30 p.m. ET on Wednesday). The attackers were shooting as they walked through the campus. The Red Cross said they stopped at a dorm for girls. At one point, they broke into a room where Christians were praying and took people hostage, said lecturer Joel Ayora.

A white casket was at the front of New Shiloh Baptist Church in West Baltimore while a gospel choir sang for a large crowd. people came to honor Freddie Gray. Gray, 25, died 15 days earlier while in police custody after being arrested on a weapons charge. He died from a serious spinal cord injury, which caused anger toward the Baltimore Police Department. His death is part of a recent series of high-profile cases involving Black people and police. Many people are asking what really happened to Gray. His funeral was attended by civil rights leaders, politicians, and family members of others who died in police custody.

I’ve been working in food since I was 14. But I didn’t start fighting for food justice until 2007. That year, a young girl my wife was mentoring was found digging in the trash just to find food. That moment changed me. I created Food Policy Action and started getting involved in food issues like hunger and factory farming. I wasn’t alone. A big turning point was "The Meatrix," a 2003 video parody of "The Matrix" made by the GRACE Communications Foundation. It clearly showed how dangerous factory farming is to people’s health and the environment.

CNN's Dan Swangard knows what death looks like. As a doctor, he has seen patients die in hospitals, on morphine, and feeling scared. He’s seen people suffer for weeks or months while family members watch helplessly. But now, his thoughts about dying have become personal. In 2013, he was diagnosed with a rare type of cancer that has spread. To treat it, doctors removed parts of his pancre and liver, as well as his whole spleen and gallbladder. The surgery worked, but Swangard, who is 48, knows there’s a high chance the cancer will come back.

CNN reported that Saudi special forces helped Yemeni fighters fight against the Houthis and their allies in Aden. A Saudi source told CNN that the special forces were on the ground in non-com战斗 roles, helping to coordinate and direct the fighting. They also assisted in dropping weapons and communication equipment by parachute. The Houthis had previously taken control of the presidential palace and other important areas in Aden, but after heavy Saudi airstrikes, they pulled back from those locations. This retreat marked a shift from their earlier gains the day before.

A Detroit mother was arrested last month after police found the bodies of two of her children in a freezer.. She was brought to court this week and was charged with murder and torture. Wayne County Prosecutor Kym Worthy said the mother, Mitchelle Angela Blair, is accused of killing her 13-year-old daughter, Stoni Ann Blair, and her 9-year-old son, Stephen Gage Berry. The bodies were discovered on March 24 by a bailiff during a court-ordered eviction. The bodies were wrapped in plastic and were found inside the freezer. The Wayne County medical examiner said Stoni died from multiple blunt force injuries, and Stephen died from multiple blunt force injuries and also from heat injuries.

Wladimir Klitschko, the world heavyweight boxing champion, has an important fight coming up on April 25 in New York against American boxer Bryant Jennings. But he is still deeply troubled by the war in his home country, Ukraine. Speaking from his training base in Miami, Klitschko said he is shocked and upset by what is happening. He said Ukraine is suffering because of Russia’s actions, even though Ukraine did not start the conflict. He added that Russia is the one that has been aggressive.

Michael Keaton hosted "Saturday Night Live" for the third time this weekend. He joked in his opening monologue about how much has changed since he first hosted in 199999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999

Just over a month ago, Kamron Taylor was found guilty of murder in an Illinois court. Early Wednesday morning, he was in an Illinois jail. He was hiding outside his cell, waiting to attack. When he struck, his victim was a jail guard on duty, according to Kankakee County Sheriff Timothy Bukowski. Taylor attacked the guard, put on the guard’s uniform, and took his keys. He then walked out of the jail and got into the guard’s brown 2012 Chevrolet Equinox SUV. The 23-year-old man, who had been scheduled to be sentenced in May, is still missing. The SUV was found around 8:30 a.m. (9:30 a.m.)

A New York City detective has been suspended after being accused of stealing $3,000 during a raid on illegal cigarettes. Police spokesman Stephen Davis confirmed the accusation. Surveillance video from CNN's affiliate News 12 Brooklyn shows Detective Ian Cyrus putting cash into a bag before leaving the Yemen Deli and Grocery store in Brooklyn last Friday. The detectives had arrested two employees for selling loose cigarettes. The store's manager, Ali Abdullah, noticed the money was missing from a box. At first, he thought one of his employees took it. But when he checked the security footage, he was shocked to see the detective taking the money. He told News 12 Brooklyn he couldn't believe what he saw.

London (CNN) – A major robbery at a well-known London safe deposit company over the holiday weekend has become known as the Hatton Garden heist. Thieves used powerful cutting tools and rappelling gear to break into the company’s vault. The company is 60 years old and located in central London. The thieves may have had up to four days to search through the boxes, which held an unknown number of items. They are believed to have stolen gems and cash worth hundreds of thousands of pounds. One former police officer thinks they may have taken as much as 200 million pounds (about $300 million).

On April 2, South Africa will mark the anniversary of its first post-apartheid elections in 1994. At the same time, there is a new wave of violent attacks against African migrants. People are angry about this violence and are speaking out on social media using the hashtag #WeAreAfrica, showing that many believe a united response is needed. These repeated attacks on migrants and their belongings suggest that South Africa’s dream of a united, diverse nation may not be coming true. That dream was about a country where people of all races and backgrounds could live with dignity.

In 1989, Ayatollah Khomeini said he was " drinkingin' poison" when he agreed to a ceasefire that ended the eight-year war with Iraq. The war had played a big role in shaping Khomeini's government, the Islamic Republic, which he had created just a year before Saddam Hussein invaded Iran. Khomeini inspired both his supporters and growing critics to fight against Iraq. He kept the war going for eight years, even though Saddam wanted to stop. This helped keep his government strong. But by the time he ended the war, the economy was ruined, and many of his loyal fighters were gone.

CNN says that the idea of sustainable development comes from the fact that raw capitalism is too strong and harmful to itself. The global economy is growing very fast, doubling in size every generation. But Earth has limited resources, and every 15 years, a billion more people are added. This rapid growth is now damaging the planet’s natural systems and the social systems that make life good and fair. Sustainable development is a way to solve this worsening crisis. The truth is that raw capitalism is based on greed.

The United States has benefited greatly from being a space-faring nation. Space has helped protect national security, support the military, and boost the economy. To handle today’s and future conflicts, fight terrorism, and deal with growing global threats, the U.S. military depends on space systems like spy satellites, GPS, and communication satellites. But there's a serious problem: as threats around the world grow and the need for reliable access to space gets stronger, the U.S. still depends too much on Russian technology to carry out its security duties.

On the one-year anniversary of when nearly 300 schoolgirls were kidnapped by Boko Haram in Nigeria, Malala Yousafzai sent an open letter. She wrote that like the kidnapped girls, she was also targeted by militants who didn't want girls to go to school. Malala, a 17-year-old Nobel Peace Prize winner, survived a Taliban attack in Pakistan after she spoke publicly about the need for girls to stay in school. She also urged the Nigerian government and the world to do more to find and rescue the girls. Nigeria had just held an election recently.

Johannesburg (CNN) – South African troops were sent in on Tuesday evening as part of a new government plan to stop violent attacks against immigrants. Their first stop was the Johannesburg suburb of Jeppestown, where the violence started on Friday. Police raided a hostel in Jeppestown on Tuesday, while troops guarded the area. Earlier, Defense Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula said the government would send an unknown number of troops to places where police are too stretched to stop deadly attacks on immigrants. "This intervention is not an indictment on the police. ..."

Eight Iranian border guards were killed in fights with armed militants near the border with Pakistan, Iranian state media said. Three of the militants were killed by Iranian forces on Monday in the town of Negur, in southeastern Iran. The Iranian news agency IRNA said the militants had crossed into Iran from Pakistan. Iranian officials have asked Pakistani authorities to find and arrest the remaining attackers.

CNN. If you love island-hopping, take note: Providenciales in the Turks and Caicos has been named the world’s best island by TripAdvisor. It moved up one spot from last year’s second place to take the top spot, replacing Ambergris Caye. in Belize. which had been number one for two years. This year, Ambergris Caye fell out of the top 10 entirely. TripAdvisor spokeswoman Julie Cassetina said it's hard to know why the rankings change each year, since they are based on traveler feedback.

The "Star Wars" universe is growing. At the Star Wars Celebration fan festival in Anaheim, California, on Sunday, details about the 2016 movie "Star Wars: Rogue One" were revealed. Director Gareth Edwards, who also directed "Godzilla," showed a short teaser for the film. He also shared plot details for this "Star Wars" anthology movie, which Disney calls instead of "spinoff." It stars Felicity Jones. The story takes place between "Episode III: Revenge of the Sith" and "Episode IV: A New Hope" — the first "Star Wars" movie from 1977. A group of rebels is on a secret mission to steal the plans for the Death Star. Felicity Jones will play a rebel soldier.

Tehran, Iran (CNN) – There is a Persian saying: "A good year is determined by its spring." Many Iranians see the recent decision by Tehran and six world powers — the U.S., UK, France, Germany, Russia, and China — to continue nuclear talks under a "joint comprehensive plan of action" as a sign that this year’s Norouz, the Persian New Year that began on March 2nd, will be a very good one. Even though some tough, conservative voices may complain that the initial agreement isn’t exactly what they wanted, most people see it as real progress — and that’s what they care about.

Ferguson, Missouri (CNN) – At 11:45 p.m. ET, two African-Americans, Ella Jones and Wesley Bell, won a seat on the Ferguson City Council. This means three of the six council members are now Black. [Earlier, at 6:52 p.m. ET] – The sky became dark and the radio was full of warnings about flash floods. Rain fell as Ferguson opened its polling places at 6 a.m. for the city’s regular election. Usually, not many people vote. But this time was different. It was the first city election since white police officer Darren Wilson shot and killed unarmed Black teenager Michael Brown in August. Since then, Ferguson has been under national attention.

One Israeli man was killed and another was injured in what police believe was a suspected terror attack Wednesday night near Hebrew University in Jerusalem. Police said a 37-year-old Arab man from East Jerusalem drove into two people waiting at a bus stop in the French Hill area. The victim, identified as Shalom Yohai Cherki, 26, died at the hospital. A 20-year-old woman is still in serious condition. The driver has been arrested and is being investigated by Israel's General Security Services.

An art collection owned by the late Hollywood star Lauren Bacall has been put up for sale.. The collection, which includes pieces by major 200th-century artists, was auctioned in New York on March 31. Before the auction, it was shown in Hong Kong, Paris, London, and Los Angeles. Bacall, who died in August 2014 at age 89, first became famous in 1944 with her film debut in "To Have and Have Not." film. She also met her future husband, Humphrey Bogart, in that same year. In 2015, at the Golden Globes, George Clooney honored Bacall in his award speech.

Kiev, Ukraine (CNN) – People in Kiev are asking: Who is killing people who were close to Ukraine’s former president, Viktor Yanukovych? This question isn’t new, but it came back into focus this week after two high-profile killings in the capital. One was Oleg Kalashnikov, a former member of parliament who was linked to Yanukovych. He was shot dead just after 7 p.m. on Wednesday at the entrance of his apartment building. The other was a Ukrainian journalist known for supporting Russia.

Same-sex civil unions will soon be recognized in Chile. President Michelle Bachelet signed a new law on Monday that allows these unions. This makes Chile one of several South American countries to allow them. Bachelet said the law is a step toward ending the difference between gay and straight couples. The law will start in six months. It will give legal rights to couples living together, whether they are two men, two women, or a man and a woman. The government says about 2 million people will benefit from this change.

When you fly to visit Grandma in Florida, look down. When you take the kids to see the talking mouse or go to South Beach for sun and fun, sit by the window and think about what you see below as you land. Because few places show how people have made big mistakes—and how hard it is to fix them—like the Everglades. As you fly into Miami or Orlando, it may look like a wet, ugly wasteland full of dangerous animals: snakes, scorpions, rats, roaches, alligators, and mosquitoes. One researcher caught 365,00 mosquitoes in one trap in just one night.

CNN reported that ISIS fighters took over Yarmouk, a Palestinian refugee camp near Damascus. Masked men flooded the streets of this already suffering area. For over two years, the camp had been under siege and bombing by Syrian forces. In early April, residents woke up to a new and even worse situation: ISIS had taken control after defeating several local militia groups. One resident, who did not want to be named, told CNN, "They killed them in the streets." He said ISIS caught three people and killed them right in front of others. Now, ISIS controls almost all of the camp.

China's internet censors have long used the "Great Firewall" to block Chinese people from reading critical articles from Western news sites or viewing other content they don’t approve of.. But now, according to a study released on Friday, they’ve created a new tool. This new system, called the "Great Cannon," attacks servers outside China, including in the United States. The study’s authors say this new weapon is used openly and directly. By attacking foreign servers so clearly and easily, China may be inviting criticism from other countries. The authors believe Beijing might have expected this reaction.

The investigation into the crash of Germanwings Flight 9525 has not found any proof of why co-pilot Andreas Lubitz crashed the plane. but a spokesman for the prosecutor's office in Dusseldorf, Germany, said Lubitz had shown signs of suicidal thoughts at some point before he started his flying career................ The prosecutor's office said that investigators have not found any notes or talks where Lubitz explained his reasons or admitted to planning the crash. But medical records show that Lubitz was suicidal at one time and had therapy for it. This happened before he got his pilot's license, the spokesman said.

The leader of Yemen's Houthi rebels said on Sunday that his fighters would not leave major cities or government buildings. He told a TV audience, "Anyone who thinks we will give up is just dreaming." His statement followed over three weeks of airstrikes by a Saudi-led coalition. The bombings were meant to stop the Houthis, who took control of the capital, Sanaa, in January and forced President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi to flee.

On April 19, 1995, Timothy McVeigh set a bomb in a truck. He exploded it in front of the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City. The blast killed 168 people, including men, women, and children, and injured many others. This attack is still the worst case of domestic terrorism in U.S. history. After the bombing, there was a lot of media coverage. Some reports said it was an "attack on the heartland" and that America had lost its " innocence." The bombing shocked the nation. It wasn't just how big the tragedy was. It was also surprising because it was the first time a U.S. citizen had attacked their own government with such deadly force.

If you really cared about something, would you protest? Would you make a sign? Join a march? How long could you keep doing that if no one else seemed to care? A year ago, over 200 Nigerian schoolgirls were kidnapped from their school by Boko Haram fighters. Millions of people worldwide responded by joining a social media campaign to demand their safe return. Charles Alasholuyi was one of them — along with celebrities and world leaders, people used the hashtag #BringBackOurGirls. It became one of the most popular Twitter hashtags of 2014, used in over four million tweets. But as weeks turned into months, the girls still weren’t found. The attention to the campaign slowly disappeared.

Barney Frank, who has a lot of experience in politics, recently spoke in Chicago to a full crowd at the Center on Halsted. He shared stories from his four years in public office. Frank was the first member of Congress to marry someone of the same sex while still in office. He also spoke strongly against politicians who hide their sexuality and vote against LGBT rights. When someone in the audience asked about a California ballot measure that would allow killing gay people, Frank said he didn’t know about the proposal. He told the young man not to worry about "the crazy people."

A violent attack on Garissa University College in Kenya has killed almost 50 people, including students, and left many others injured. The gunmen attacked the campus early Thursday morning during morning prayers, shooting randomly and taking hostages before being killed by security forces. The U.S. Embassy in Nairobi said Al-Shabaab is responsible for the attack. This comes just months after Al-Shabaab killed non-Muslim workers at a quarry in Kenya. The group has carried out many attacks in the region and has recruited some Americans, especially from the Somali-American community in Minnesota.

A South African university is celebrating the removal of a statue of British colonialist Cecil Rhodes, after weeks of protests. Students at the University of Cape Town used social media to demand the statue be taken down, saying Rhodes' legacy is linked to racism. They started a campaign using the hashtag #RhodesMustFall. Four weeks later, the hashtag has changed to #RhodesHasFallen. The university said on Wednesday that a heritage authority gave permission to remove the statue. The university added that the removal is to keep the statue safe while decisions are made about its future.

CNN says Syria is like hell and is getting worse. The number of people killed there has doubled in one year, according to an opposition group. Since the civil war started, 310,000 people have died, according to the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights (SOHR). A year ago, SOHR reported 162240000 deaths. The year before that, the United Nations said about 70,000 had died. The UN says more than half of all Syrians are now in such desperate poverty that they need urgent help to survive. This is because food rations are being reduced due to not enough donations.

(Ailina Tsarnaeva walked into Manhattan Criminal Court quietly and appeared shy. But prosecutors say she was not afraid to threaten a woman she saw as a rival. In a phone call this summer, she told the woman, "Leave my man alone. Stop looking for him." She also said, "I know people that can put a bomb where you live," according to a criminal complaint. Because of who she is — the sister of Dzhokhar and Tamerlan Tsarnaev — prosecutors took the threat seriously and charged her with aggravated harassment. She denies the charge. Last December, after leaving court, she and her lawyer refused to talk about the case.

A door painted with graffiti by British artist Banksy was taken by police in Gaza on Thursday after a dispute over its sale, a Gaza police official told CNN. The door’s owner, Rabea Darduna, said he didn’t know it was valuable and sold it for just $175 U.S. The iron door is now being held by the Khan Younis police in southern Gaza. It will stay there until a court hearing, which has not yet been scheduled. Darduna said his home in Gaza was destroyed during last summer’s war, and he felt he had nothing left—only a doorway and a door.

CNN reported that the fighting against the Houthis rebels in Yemen continued on Tuesday. The Saudi-led coalition said it was gaining more control, as people fled the violence and the death toll rose — including many civilians. Five days after their first airstrikes, the coalition had destroyed most of the Houthis' air defense systems and those of allies of Yemen's former president, Ali Abdullah Saleh. They also made almost all air bases and runways unusable, according to a Saudi source. Saudi Arabia's navy now controls all Yemeni ports. Only non-military medical supplies are allowed through the blockade, and they are closely monitored.

Holland's manager Guus Hiddink criticized his own fans for booing Spain's Andres Iniesta during Holland's 2-0 win over Spain on Tuesday. He said the fans' behavior was a "disgrace." Iniesta played for Spain, who used a young and experimental team. He came on in the 76th minute but was met with loud boos from the home crowd. at the Amsterdam Arena.......... The goals were scored by Holland's Stefan de Vrij and Davy Klaassen in the first half, helping Holland win. But Hiddink was angry about how Iniesta was treated. Iniesta is a Spain player who was on the field during the match.

On May 21, Scotland will find out if their Euro 2016 qualifier against Georgia in September will be played without fans. UEFA has started disciplinary action against the Georgian Football Federation (GFF) after fans ran onto the pitch twice during Georgia's 2-0 loss to Germany in Tbilisi on Sunday. UEFA will also investigate reports that home fans used fireworks, and safety problems at the Boris Paichadze Stadium, such as blocked stairs, locked gates, and staff not doing body searches. One fan ran onto the pitch during the match.

On Wednesday, football agents were unsure what to expect while waiting for new rules. Starting April 1, anyone can become a football agent by paying £500 for a one-year registration. The FA will then charge £250 each year to renew. Agents who were already licensed do not have to pay the fee. The FA was supposed to put a link on its website so intermedi can register, but as of 1pm, that link was still not there. Mel Stein believes the new rules will cause chaos. The new rules came after FIFA stopped overseeing football agents.

Maksims Uvarenko, a Latvian goalkeeper for financially struggling CSKA Sofia, hasn't been paid in three months. He had to ask his parents to send him money to pay his rent. Even though he's facing money problems, Uvarenko said he's impressed by the fans' passionate support. He joined CSKA Sofia in January on a 8-month contract. He told local media that the lack of money is his biggest problem. He still hasn't received any salary after being at the club for three months.

David Moore, 25, lost control and attacked another driver after leaving his home. He got stuck in heavy traffic on a busy street and came face to face with Rafal Cegielka, 45, who was picking up his child from St John's Primary School in Burnley, Lancashire. Moore then punched the father and broke his car with a hockey stick, all in front of young children. He did this because he was having a bad day and said he "sed red." The court heard these details.

Spain lost 2-0 to Holland on Tuesday, reminding people of their poor performance at the 2014 World Cup. But defender Gerard Piqué says coach Vicente del Bosque shouldn’t be too worried about this third straight friendly loss.
