A large fire burned through dry heathland near the south coast. Flames jumped high and thick smoke rose into the sky. The fire destroyed an area about the size of 100 football fields. This happened after several days of storms in Britain, which had knocked down trees and blocked roads. But the 70-hectare area in Dorset was very dry because it is on a hillside and water had run off. Fire investigators said the fire was started on purpose. Three separate areas of heath were burned: one was half a hectare, one was one hectare, and one was 70 hectares.

Emergency services got 600 calls every hour last night as people across Britain celebrated the New Year. Paramedics were very busy. In Cambridge, a field hospital from the Territorial Army was set up to help drunk partygoers. The London Ambulance Service said they had more than 600 calls per hour at the busiest time, which is over three times more than usual.  
 In Manchester, a man fell down on the pavement next to an ambulance while two people walked past eating a late-night takeaway. In another scene in Manchester, a man was leaning against a doorway, looking very unwell, while two women walked by celebrating the New Year.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet said his mental strength helped him get through being dropped by manager Brendan Rodgers in December. Mignolet was left out of the team indefinitely after a run of poor performances. He returned quickly when backup keeper Brad Jones got a thigh injury. The 27-year-old Belgian said he stayed positive even though he was upset about losing his place. Mignolet made a save from a free kick in a recent match against Swansea. He told FourFourTwo: "I was positive."

Large hailstones, about the size of plums, fell over the southern U.S. on Tuesday. People ran outside to record the unusual weather. Arke USA, a Twitter user from Bryant, Arkansas, filmed the hail hitting his backyard and bouncing into his swimming pool. The video shows the hail falling fast, with many breaking apart when they hit the ground. Even though the temperature was around 80 degrees, the hard hailstones didn’t melt quickly. Within seconds, the patio was completely covered in white hail pellets.

A group of nine people on a replica pirate schooner called the Liana's Ransom had to leave their ship after it lost power in heavy seas off the coast of Maine. The Coast Guard rescued them on Tuesday. The ship, which is from Canada, was left floating 30 miles east of Portland. The crew said their engines stopped working around 12:35 a.m. on Monday. They also said the sails had gotten caught around the mast. The Coast Guard sent life boats to help, and the crew had to jump from the ship into the boats.

Strange blue glowing algae have been seen along Australia’s east coast. The photos were taken in Jervis Bay, on the south coast of New South Wales, showing the bright blue light on a popular beach. Photographer Andy Hutchinson called the scene "a beautiful, otherworldly sight" caused by millions of tiny plankton giving off light. A similar glow was seen at Sydney’s Manly Beach in August 2014. An oceanography expert told Daily Mail Australia there was no reason to worry about the algae.

A 17-year-old boy named Rahul Kumar was drunk when he climbed into the lion enclosure at the Kamla Nehru Zoological Park in Ahmedabad, India. He was sitting near the fence when he suddenly ran toward the lions, shouting, "Today I kill a lion!" He had been drinking and said later he thought he could fight the lions. Zoo security saw him and quickly rescued him.

A 2-year-old boy in Nanchang, the capital of Jiangxi Province in southeastern China, survived after falling out of a fifth-floor window. He landed on a car parked below. His father said the boy likely fell while sleepwalking. The incident happened last Saturday. A hotel worker across the street said she heard a loud noise around midnight and thought it was a car crash. The car helped save the boy’s life.

Drew Miller of the Red Wings says he’s ready to play again just one day after getting a serious cut to his face that could have damaged his eyesight.. " said he felt very lucky the skate didn’t hit his eye. "I feel very blessed," he said at practice on Wednesday. Miller was skating with a full face mask. The cut was deep and needed 5 to 60 stitches to close. It went through several layers of skin. The Detroit Free Press reported that the injury left a visible scar across his eye. However, he did not lose any eyesight, even though another player cut him across the face.

Filipe Luis says he wants to stay at Chelsea until his contract ends, even though Atletico Madrid might try to bring him back in the summer. He signed a three-year deal when he moved from Atletico last July, but hasn’t been able to secure the left-back spot at Chelsea. Atletico hopes this could help them get him back, but Luis says, “I’m happy at Chelsea. I want to stay at the club until the end of my contract.”

A Reading football fan, Charlie Sumner, 20, could get banned from football for three years after he ran onto the pitch topless during his first ever game at Madejski Stadium.......... The game was against Bradford City in the FA Cup quarter-final replay, and Reading were winning 3-0 at the time. Sumner did four front somersaults on the pitch, landing on his back, before being stopped by stewards. He said going to his first game was a " brilliant experience," but now faces a possible three-year ban for his actions.

A video has been released showing a dangerous moment when a van carrying several men on its roof lost control and flipped onto its side. while turning sharply on a road near Salé, Morocco. About six people were riding on top of the van when it tipped over at high speed. The video, filmed from a car behind the van, shows the vehicle weaving back and forth on a busy road, likely a dual carriway. The van is believed to have been carrying football fans.

England have been placed in Group D of the UEFA Under-17 European Championships, which will be held in Bulgaria in May. The group also includes the Republic of Ireland, Holland, and Italy. England are the defending champions after winning last year’s tournament in Malta by beating Holland in a penalty shootout. To reach the quarter-finals, England will need to beat Holland again. This year’s tournament has expanded from eight to 16 teams, making it bigger than ever. Danny Collinge celebrated by running away after scoring his first goal for England in a qualifying match against Norway.

An angry elephant sprayed water from its trunk at a buffalo bull that got too close while the elephant was resting with its family near a small pool in Kruger National Park, South Africa. The elephant was trying to scare the bull away, but missed. The video shows the elephant trying again, clearly annoyed. Nearby, a baby elephant stayed close to its mother for safety, while the bull drank from the pool.

Michael Thorpe, a former pub landlord, has had his conviction overturned after eight years. He was originally found guilty in November 2006 for showing a Premier League football match on a foreign TV channel at the Stoke Inn in Plymouth, Devon. He had no agreement with the official broadcasters. Mr Thorpe, 55, says the long legal fight has cost him dearly—he lost his pub and suffered a heavy personal price. He has now won his battle to clear his name.

The Irish Football Association hopes that damage to its home stadium, Windsor Park in Belfast, won’t stop the team from playing its important Euro 2016 qualifier against Romania in June. on Tuesday morning, workers found cracks in the West Stand. The area was closed off while engineers checked the damage. An IFA spokesman said the association learned about the damage on Tuesday morning. The West Stand at Windsor Park was damaged overnight on Monday.

A football fan is at risk of a three-year ban after running topless onto the pitch and doing several somersaults during his first visit to a stadium.. Charlie Sumner, 20, broke onto the field at Reading's Madejski Stadium during the FA Cup quarter-final replay against Bradford City last month. He did four front flips on the grass, landing on his back each time, while Reading were leading 3-0. He was then stopped by stadium staff.

A man driving a BMW with five children in the car was arrested today after a young student, Hina Shamim, 2, was hit and killed while walking to the library. Hina died near the University of Kingston in London last night, just weeks before her second birthday. People who knew her left flowers at the scene. Hina, who was from Peterborough and had the nickname "Hyena," was described by friends as "much-loved" and "the most charming lovely girl in the world." She was killed after being hit while walking a short way from her home to the library.

A mother and her teenage daughter were arrested after a video showed them fighting with a student at Langham Creek High School in Houston.. The incident happened on Tuesday and was caught on camera. The mother, whose name has not been made public, was upset because she believed the student had been bullying her daughter. In the video, the mother is wearing a black top on the right side, and the student, who was attacked, is in the center wearing white. The video was posted online and later reported by Channel 2.

Stoke chief executive Tony Scholes hopes the club can keep goalkeeper Asmir Begovic, as he nears the end of his contract. The Bosnia international has often been linked with other clubs since joining Stoke. His current contract runs for just over two months, but Scholes believes Stoke can meet Begovic’s goals and ambitions. "Asmir is a top goalkeeper, and we really want him to stay," Scholes said. "It's normal for good players to attract interest, so there will always be talk about their future."

A bus driver in Auckland, New Zealand, was strongly criticized by his boss after being caught on video reading a newspaper while driving. A passenger filmed the driver during the trip and sent the video to the bus company, Ritchies Coachlines, along with a complaint. In the video, the driver is seen turning the pages of a newspaper while the bus is moving. At a traffic light, he even turns his head to read a page more clearly. The company’s boss, Andrew Ritchie, said he was embarrassed by the driver’s behavior and called him a "complete idiot."

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce has said Winston Reid will be fit for Saturday's game against Leicester City, who are at the bottom of the league.. But Enner Valencia will not play. Reid missed the match on March 4 when he hurt his hamstring in a 1-0 loss to Chelsea. He has now returned to full training during the international break. Valencia missed West Ham's last two games against Arsenal and Sunderland. He got a strange toe injury at home in mid-March. But Allardyce says Valencia is still not ready to play. Allardyce confirmed: "We've got Winston back in full training."

Five days before Brittany Huber and John Redman were supposed to get married last May, a terrible car accident on a Georgia highway killed Brittany and left John badly injured. John survived, but his body was severely damaged. Doctors told him he would probably spend the rest of his life in a nursing home, unable to walk. He was 25. and worked as an assistant basketball coach at Dalton State College. Even though things looked very bad, John got better. On March 24, he helped his team win a championship.

Lucas (on the left) was seen with Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard during Sunday’s All-Star charity game at Anfield. Lucas Leiva, a Liverpool midfielder, is trying to get back to his best form after being injured. He had 16 starts in 19 games from late November, which was when Liverpool’s results got much better. But he missed 10 games after a groin injury in February’s Merseyside derby. Before the international break, he sat on the bench in the loss to Manchester United — the first league game since mid-December. But he played the full 90 minutes in Sunday’s charity game at Anfield.

Tired of boring father-daughter photos? One photographer has come up with a strange but fun way to make them better. Japanese photographer Yûki Aoyama took a series of photos showing serious teenagers standing next to their dads, who are jumping in the air. In each photo, the daughter looks straight at the camera and smiles, while her father makes a dramatic pose. These photos are from Aoyama’s new book, which is about 37 years old and roughly means "Daughter and Salary Man."

Police are looking for a man between 50 and 60 years old. He is 5ft 9in to 6ft tall and was wearing black clothes. He is believed to have robbed a Lloyds Bank in Fairwater, Cardiff, at 12.300 in the afternoon. He took £3,000 in cash. The man had greying black hair and wore glasses. He was seen on CCTV inside the bank. No one was hurt during the robbery. Police are confident the public can help identify him.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has removed Morocco's ban from the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments.. The country was originally kicked out of the 2017 and 2019 tournaments and fined $1 million by the Confederation of African Football (CAF). CAF also wanted Morocco to pay $9 million more in compensation, after Morocco withdrew as host due to fears about the Ebola virus. Morocco had pulled out as host of the African Cup of Nations, which was won by Ivory Coast in Equatorial Guinea. Now, Morocco is allowed to take part in the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments after the ban was lifted..

Tom Boyd thinks Jason Denayer has done so well during his loan at Celtic that he is now ready to fight for a spot at Manchester City next season... This might go against Celtic manager Ronny Deila’s plan to keep Denayer for another year, but Boyd sees a good side to it. He believes Denayer’s progress can help attract more young players to join Celtic. The 19-year-old defender has played well on loan at Celtic this season. He also earned his first senior international cap for Belgium in a Euro 2016 qualifier against Cyprus.

Andros Townsend scored a great goal for England, silencing his critics. He said critics like Paul Merson helped push him to do well, especially during his time in Italy. This season has been tough for the 23-year-old player, who hasn't reached the same level he showed when he first played for England. But manager Roy Hodgson still believed in him. That faith was rewarded in a big way at Juventus Stadium. Townsend scored England’s equalizer in a 1-1 friendly draw against Italy on Tuesday night. He celebrated the goal with his Tottenham teammates, Ryan Mason and Kyle Walker.

Chinese property company Dalian Wanda Group has officially bought 20% of Atletico Madrid. The deal was confirmed at an Extraordinary General Meeting on Tuesday. Wanda Madrid Investment’s legal team signed the agreement to buy 726,707 shares for €45 million (£32.8 million). The initial agreement was announced in January, but it was made after two EGMs. Wanda Group chairman Wang Jianlin wants to grow Atletico's brand in Asia. Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone is speaking to reporters.

Antonio Conte says he was back in Turin for Italy's 1-1 draw with England, and it brought back happy memories, even though he had been threatened with death before the game. Conte became Italy's manager in August after the national team failed to get past the group stage of the World Cup. His first seven months as manager have been very difficult. Italy needed a late goal from Eder to tie Bulgaria 2-2 last Saturday. Conte was also said to have received death threats from Juventus fans after Claudio Marchisio got a knee injury the day before a Euro 2016 qualifier.

Ian Murray thinks that a potentially easier schedule could help Hibs overtake Rangers for second place in the Championship. in the final month of the season. His Dumbarton team has already played both of his former clubs this season and will face them again in the closing weeks. Although Rangers are currently in better form— having beaten Hibs and Cowdenbeath, while Hibs lost to Raith—Murray doesn’t think Hibs will stay behind for long. He also believes Rangers won’t be able to keep up their current pace through the final part of the season.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet took photos with pilots in an airplane cockpit when he returned to England after playing for Belgium in the Euro 2006 qualifiers against Cyprus and Israel.. He was named in the match-day squad for both games, but did not play because Chelsea goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois was chosen instead. Mignolet has 14 international caps. He shared the photos from the cockpit on his Facebook page on Wednesday. The picture shows Mignolet (in the middle) standing with the pilots.

A large country estate, including a Grade II-listed manor house and five cottages, is for sale for £6 million. It sits on 200 acres of land near Bridgnorth in Shropshire. The estate has a swimming pool, tennis court, stables, and a cricket field. The main house, Chyknell Hall, has 11111 bedrooms and was built in 1814. It has only had two owners since then. The Regney-style house could appeal to famous people because the private grounds offer full seclusion. The estate is on the market for £6 million.

Two campus police officers in Dallas have been put on administrative leave after video showed them mistreating a group of four students and arresting one after hitting him. The incident happened at El Centro College. Student Charles Adams filmed the event on his phone. He was smoking a cigarette when he saw what happened. The officers approached the students, who were high schoolers waiting for a bus, outside the downtown Dallas campus. The video is below.

Kilmarnock's interim manager Gary Locke has been made permanent after signing a three-year contract. The 39-year-old former Hearts manager joined the club last summer as assistant to Allan Johnston. He took charge when Johnston left in early February. Since then, Locke has lost only once in seven games. He will speak to the media at a press conference on Friday morning. After the deal was confirmed, Locke shook hands with chairman Jim Mann.

One of the most important games in German football happens this weekend. Borussia Dortmund and Bayern Munich have won the last five Bundesliga titles between them. Bayern are expected to keep winning the league this season. But this time, the two top teams are not close in the standings. They are three points apart and nine places apart in the rankings. Still, the game is just as important as ever. These two clubs always play with high stakes. Jurgen Klopp (center) celebrates with his Borussia Dortmund players after beating Hannover.

A 14-year-old schoolgirl was left at a busy airport after easyJet refused to let her board her flight to Spain. She was carrying two bags as hand luggage. Deva Joseph cried at London Stansted Airport when she was told she couldn't fly. She offered to pay to check her second bag, but was told only credit cards would be accepted—even though she is too young to have one.

Gordon Robson, 26, killed his grandfather, John Potts, 45, with one hard punch to the back of the head. The punch was so strong it made a loud cracking sound. The incident happened after Robson had been drinking at his grandfather's funeral. He hit John Potts, a devoted father, outside a sports bar in Washington, Tyne and Wear. The attack occurred in November last year. Robson had a history of violent behavior. He was sentenced to three and a half years in prison for the killing.

Scoring against your old team and making a perfect set-piece from training are two of the best moments in football. and Notts County player Ellen White had both happen in one game. On Thursday night, she scored against Arsenal in the Women's Super League. In the 26th minute, Notts County got a free kick near the box. Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood nearly collided, causing confusion. Then Ellen White turned near the box and kicked the ball straight into the corner of the goal, scoring against her former team.

High school girls in China are doing military-style dagger drills. They shout words like "kill, stab, slash, and jab" as they do eight fixed movements in a fast, intense training session. The girls, aged 16 to 18, are from the 27th March Huizhou Integrated High School. They are being trained by Inspector Tan, a former special forces soldier. The knives used are not real. A school official, Huang Anruo, confirmed: "The daggers are fake."

We spend about one-third of our lives sleeping, but many of us don’t think about what our mind and body really need during sleep to feel rested each day.. The Sleep Health Foundation shared a study showing that 3 in 10 Australians say they don’t get enough sleep every day. Professor David Hillman, the chair, says missing sleep must be made up to stay healthy and active all week. The study also found that 3 in 10 Australians say they don’t get enough sleep every day. Most adults need about eight hours of sleep each night, and seven to nine hours is considered normal.

A video has been shared on Facebook showing a fight between neighbours in a Perth suburb that turned violent. The video shows an angry woman yelling racist insults over a fence at a group of men she seems to believe are of African descent. She then goes into her neighbour’s yard, holds a metal crowbar, shouts at the men, and swings the tool at them. The men respond by grabbing their own weapons, and a fight breaks out. The woman shouts, “I don’t deal with monkeys — go on, you f*****g monkeys.”

A lot of people are watching 19-year-old Valencia left back Jose Luis Gaya. He’s attracting interest from big English clubs like Manchester City, Arsenal, and Chelsea. They want to sign him this summer, even though Real Madrid also have a link to him. Gaya is a Spanish under-21s player. His current buy-out clause is £13.5 million. That’s a key reason why English clubs are interested. For comparison, Luke Shaw, who is a similar age and talent level, cost £27 million. So getting Gaya for £13.5 million seems like a good deal. However, there are still concerns about whether he’s ready for the Premier League. Gaya played for Valencia in a La Liga match against Sevilla earlier this season

Police in Oregon are asking the public for help identifying a motorcyclist who helped stop a man who allegedly threatened two teenagers with a gun.. The incident happened in Salem. The man, Edward West, 59, is accused of pointing a handgun at the teens and saying, "get ready to die." At that moment, a man on a green motorcycle arrived and used his helmet to knock the gun from the man’s hand. This allowed the teens to run away. The motorcyclist then left the scene. Police are trying to find him to thank him and share details.

Tim Sherwood is telling Ron Vlaar to show he still deserves to be Aston Villa's captain. Vlaar is coming back from injury and will play in the match against Manchester United at Old Trafford. Sherwood wants Vlaar to help the team fight hard to avoid relegation. He also warned Vlaar that people might have forgotten how he played well in the 2000 World Cup, when he helped the Netherlands reach the semi-finals, Brazil. Vlaar missed a penalty in the shoot-out against Argentina, but still made a strong impact. That performance led to rumours he might join Manchester United. Now, he’s back and needs to prove himself again.

Tim Sherwood says he is not worried about Aston Villa’s possible summer takeover. He plans to build his own team for next season, as long as the club avoids relegation. Randy Lerner is reportedly talking to a potential buyer, and if a new owner takes over, questions may arise about Sherwood’s future. But Sherwood is concentrating only on helping Villa stay in the league. After that, he will work on his long-term plans during the summer. The manager says he is not concerned about the takeover talks. Christian Benteke scored and celebrated as Aston Villa beat Sunderland last month.

Celtic have long wanted Manchester City to let Jason Denayer return on loan to Parkhead next season. But things don’t always go as planned. And that might be the case now, after Manchester City said on Thursday that their young Academy players aren’t ready to play in the first team. So, players like Denayer could be brought back early from loan deals. Denayer has done well during his loan spell at Celtic this season.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman is waiting for a clearer date for Fraser Forster's return before deciding if he needs to sign another goalkeeper in the summer. Forster had knee surgery after hurting himself in the 2-0 win over Burnley two weeks ago. His return is expected between four and 12 weeks, but Koeman isn't giving a firm date. He thinks Kelvin Davis can handle the job in the meantime, but says he might have to bring in another goalkeeper if Forster takes longer to recover. Forster got his serious knee injury during the game against Burnley a couple of weeks ago.

Rotherham manager Steve Evans was angry on the touchline during his team’s close Sky Bet Championship loss at Birmingham.. Rotherham were fighting against relegation, and they felt they should have been given a penalty. Birmingham had taken the lead in the first half through goals from Robert Tesche and Clayton Donaldson.. Matt Derbyshire scored one for Rotherham, who are fourth from bottom. Near the end of the game, Rob Kiernan handled the ball on the edge of the box while challenging Derbyshire, who fell inside the area. But referee Dean Whitestone did not give a penalty, which made Evans very upset. Birmingham then held on to win the match. Robert Tesche, a Birmingham player, celebrated his goal.

Virgil van Dijk is worrying about his chances with the Dutch national team. Holland has already let in more goals in five Euro 2016 qualifiers than they did in the whole previous World Cup qualifying campaign.. And still, Guus Hiddink hasn’t contacted him. Van Dijk was named in two squads last year, but he’s been left out again. When the Netherlands drew 1-1 with Turkey, he was relaxing in the Arabian Gulf, hanging out with former club-mates. He’s been playing well for Celtic, but hasn’t been called up to the Dutch national team.

Celtic have complained to the SFA about the ticket prices for their Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness, which is happening later this month at Hampden. The match is on Sunday, April 18, at 12:15pm. This time is causing problems for fans from Inverness, as the first trains from Inverness won’t arrive in Glasgow until after the game. Ticket prices are £ 23 for the North and South stands, and £15 for adults in the East Stand, with £5 for concession tickets. Celtic are unhappy with these prices and have made their concerns known to the SFA.

Rangers' interim chairman, Paul Murray, said on Thursday that the club's removal from the stock exchange was completely due to actions taken by past board members. The club must now leave the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) because it couldn't find a new nominated advisor (Nomad) to meet rules. Murray says the new board's plans for the future are not affected, and planned investments will still happen. He repeated that past board decisions were the only reason for the club's del listing.

Wayne Rooney and his England teammates were disappointed with how they started their match against Italy on Tuesday night.  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
The game took place at Juventus Stadium in Turin. It was a friendly match, the second meeting between England and Italy in nine months, since their game at the World Cup. England had won seven games in a row, so many were hopeful of a strong performance. But in the first half, England played poorly and failed to create much. Italy scored first, with a header from Graziano Pelle. England equalized later, making the final score 1-1. After the match, Rooney said he and the other England players were upset by how they played in the first half.

Dundee United's board has responded to strong criticism from two major supporters' groups, Arabtrust and the Federation of Dundee United Supporters Clubs. The groups said they were shocked that 25% of the £6.3 million spent on transfers for Ryan Gauld, Andrew Robertson, Stuart Armstrong, and Gary Mackay-Steven was paid as commission to unknown people. They also questioned chairman Stephen Thompson's claim about how much he has invested in the club. In reply, the club's board said their success on the pitch shows their performance has been strong.

Gary Locke will be officially named Kilmarnock’s permanent manager on Friday. This is exactly eight weeks after he was asked to take over until the end of the season. He will sign a three-year contract. The club will make the announcement on Friday morning. Locke, who previously managed Hearts, replaced Allan Johnston in February on a temporary basis. He is 39 years old. He thanked the players for their hard work, which helped him gain the support of new chairman Jim Mann.

Chinese parents often want their children to become child prodigies, like 10-year-olds who go to university or four-year-olds who copy Michael Jackson's dance moves.. Now, a new young basketball star is becoming famous.. A video of a five-year-old boy doing amazing basketball moves is spreading online in China.. The boy, named Mai Zizhuo, has been playing basketball since he was two and a half, according to People's Daily Online. The video shows him scoring many baskets in a row, then running while dribming two basketballs at the same time.

Bayern Munich will miss versatile left-back David Alaba for about seven weeks due to a torn knee ligament. Alaba, who had already been out for three months earlier this season with a partial ligament tear in his right knee, got injured during Austria’s 1-1 draw against Bosnia on Tuesday.. 'I am very disappointed,' the 22-year-old said on the club’s website. 'But I have a big goal, and that is to be back for the final game of the season.' Alaba was tackled by Emir Spahic during Austria’s match against Bosnia-Herzegovina.

Hull KR have signed experienced Australian forward Dane Tilse to replace Michael Weyman and Ryan Bailey, who both left the club. Tilse, who is 6 feet 7 inches and weighs over 17 stone, has signed a two-and-a-half-year contract and will join Hull KR once he gets the required paperwork after being released by the Canberra Raiders. Tilse, 30, has played 200 games in Australia. He will play alongside his old Raiders teammate Terry Campese, who is now Hull KR captain and has just signed a two-year contract extension. Tilse is taking over Weyman’s role, as Weyman retired last month because of injury.

Livingston manager Mark Burchill thinks midfielder Darren Cole wants to play in Sunday’s Petrofac Cup final. Even though his cousin, Shaun Cole, 22, died in America just a week ago. Shaun was found dead on a Miami street and likely died in a hit-and-run accident. He was a former soldier who had served in Afghanistan and was on leave. He was in Florida for a holiday and had been to a music festival before he was found with a head injury. The injury was fatal. Darren Cole has been deeply upset by the loss. But Mark Burchill hopes Darren will play in the final on Sunday.

Alan Smith has denied reports that Liverpool fans attacked the ambulance he was in after he was seriously injured during a 2006 FA Cup match between Manchester United and Liverpool. He broke his leg and dislocated his ankle while trying to stop a free-kick by John Arne Riise. The match took place in February 2006 at Anfield. At the time, some said fans had thrown bottles, beer glasses, and stones at the ambulance, and even tried to rock it. (Note: this content may be disturbing.)

Celtic are interested in signing Hearts captain Danny Wilson this summer. He is a former Rangers and Liverpool player. Celtic may offer £400000 for him. Wilson has one year left on his contract. Hearts owner Ann Budge says the club doesn’t need to sell him, even though he is out of contract at the end of the season. Hearts are not in a hurry to sell him.

Ronny Deila says Celtic won’t risk their Champions League hopes by doing another tough pre-season tour.. The Norwegian says last summer’s series of matches in the US, Austria, and Germany hurt the team and led to a 4-1 loss in the Champions League qualifier against Legia Warsaw. Celtic earn good money from pre-season games and have also played in Australia and the Far East in recent years. Deila and player Nir Bitton left the pitch after the loss to Legia Warsaw. A return to the US this July is still possible, but not confirmed.

Franck Ribery has said that reports linking Wolfsburg's Kevin de Bruyne to a move to Bayern Munich are not true. De Bruyne, who spent two years at Chelsea mostly on loan, has scored nine goals this season and has 16 assists, the most in the Bundesliga. But Ribery says that even though De Bruyne is playing well, he’s not the right kind of player to replace him or his teammate Arjen Robben under manager Pep Guardiola. because their playing styles are different.

The girlfriend of an Arizona State University football player, Davon Durant, has now said she lied about being assaulted. She said her mood swings made her make up the story. Durant, a linebacker at ASU, was arrested on domestic violence charges after his girlfriend, Kelsi Langley, said he hit her in the face and choked her during an argument in his car on March 7. After the arrest, Durant— who came to ASU from a Kansas college and was a five-star recruit—was suspended from the football team indefinitely. He could also be expelled from school.

What could be more exciting than meeting your idol? How about meeting your idol at a Starbucks, wearing a shirt with their name on it, and having your photo posted on their Instagram? A young boy got lucky when he met Justin Verlander, the pitcher for the Detroit Tigers, in just those exact, rare moments. Verlander took a selfie with the boy, who was wearing a dark blue shirt that had Verlander’s name and his jersey number, 35, printed on the back. The photo was later shared on Verlander’s Instagram. See the video below.

Eden Hazard said that playing so many games this season might have made him too tired to play his best.. He was taken off after 62 minutes in Belgium’s 1-0 win over Israel on Tuesday. Hazard has played 48 games this season for club and country, missing only five matches for Chelsea. He was a key player in Chelsea’s push for the Premier League title. But in the game against Israel, Belgium had a tough time winning. Hazard was substituted with 28 minutes left because he was struggling to beat his opponent, Orel Dgani.. His manager, Marc Wilmots, made the decision to take him off.

Police found 20 grams of marijuana hidden inside a leg of lamb in the Northern Territory. The meat was suspicious, and was x-rayed by officers. It was believed the lamb was being sent from Darwin Airport to the Tiwi Islands, about 100kms to the north.

Former Premier League footballer Clarke Carlisle has said he has separated from his wife, Gemma, after 14 years of marriage. He lives in Yorkshire. Carlisle, who has been struggling with depression, moved out of their home. He had tried to take his life in December, just two days after being arrested on suspicion of drink-driving.

Arsenal legend Paul Merson had to admit he was wrong after criticizing Andros Townsend's call-up to the England squad. The Tottenham winger came on as a substitute and scored a brilliant goal to equalize in England's 1-1 draw against Italy in Turin. This happened just after Merson wrote in his Sky Sports column: 'If Andros Townsend can get in (the England squad) then it opens it up for anybody.' Townsend's strike was the perfect answer to his comment. The goal came in a friendly match, and Townsend celebrated with teammates Ryan Mason and Kyle Walker.

Cesc Fabregas, the Chelsea midfielder, has a habit of playing poorly in the second half of the season. He was one of the worst players on the field again in Spain’s 2-0 loss to Holland on Tuesday. The 27-year-old had said he was happy playing in southwest London earlier in the week, but his performance has dropped sharply since Christmas, when he looked like he would break the Premier League record for most assists.

Six people have been arrested in Dover this morning on suspicion of terrorism offences linked to Syria, police said. Five men and one woman were taken into custody around 8 a.m. at the departure area of the south coast port. Four of the men, all in their 20s, are from Birmingham in the West Midlands. A 26-year-old man and a 23-year-old woman, who have no fixed address, were also arrested. All six are now being questioned at a police station in the West Midlands.

Get ready to buy something — the strongest urge to treat yourself happens today at 2:52pm. A study says people in the UK spend about £62 a week on little rewards. The urge to shop for treats is strongest at lunchtime today. Things people buy as treats can be as simple as a chocolate bar or a glass of wine, or as big as designer clothes and shoes. This research was done by the website VoucherCodes.co.uk. It also found that men spend 33333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333

Arsène Wenger is so respected and clearly very smart that sometimes you agree with him, only to realize later that what he said sounds reasonable but isn’t really based on strong evidence. This often happens when he talks about Arsenal’s strong defensive record — which is true — right after a bad performance. Last week, he spoke about player quotas, especially the idea by FA chairman Greg Dyke to raise the number of homegrown players in a Premier League squad from 8 to 25.

Charlie Austin has shared how his friend Joey Barton ignored him on his first day at Queens Park Rangers, before realising he had made a mistake. Then, the two became close friends. Austin had a strong first season in the Premier League and has scored 15 goals in the competition, making him a possible candidate to play for England in the future. Although their friendship is well known, their first meeting was not a good start. Charlie Austin and Joey Barton are now good friends, even though they had a rough start.

This dog saved his owner from a cold and muddy grave. The black dog was filmed on Saturday afternoon at the Clarence J. Brown Dam and Reservoir in Springfield, Ohio, pulling a rescue rope to his owner. He had been stuck waist-deep in mud while trying to recover some duck hunting gear. The man was in water close to zero degrees Celsius for nearly two hours. He had a cell phone and called 911, but firefighters couldn’t reach him by boat because the river was too shallow. He was eventually pulled to safety by firefighters.

Juventus coach Massimiliano Allegri says he doesn't expect the fans to fully accept him until he wins a league title. He joined the team last summer, after being fired by AC Milan. Since then, he has done well, leading Juventus to a strong position at the top of Serie A. He took over from Antonio Conte. On Saturday, Juventus will play Empoli at home and aim to win their third straight point. The team is currently first in Serie A, and Allegri is coaching them from the touchline.

Nathan Redmond had only been on the field for six minutes when he made a key play in this close match.. Steven Whittaker spotted Redmond running down the right side and passed the ball just inside the touchline. Redmond used his speed to quickly beat Joe Bennett, then sent a low cross. Bradley Johnson at the back post hit the ball hard into the net. Johnson celebrated after scoring the winning goal in the second half at the Amex Stadium.

For people in Celoron, New York, the statue of local celebrity Lucile Ball is not funny. It has upset them for six years. In 2009, the town put up a statue of Ball. But her face looks very different from the real Lucile Ball. Many locals were shocked and angry. The statue looks so bad that a Facebook page called "We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue" got over 600 likes. People in Celoron say the statue looks monstrous. The statue is based on a scene from Ball's show 'I Love Lucy,' where she pretends to be drunk while selling a health tonic.

South Sydney hooker Issac Luke is facing a homophobic accusation after posting a rude comment on social media. Responding to abuse from Canterbury Bulldogs fans. The 27-year-old had posted on his Instagram on Saturday, trying to find a young Rabbitohs fan who was attacked at ANZ Stadium in Sydney. He wanted to help by giving the boy a jersey, as a kind gesture after the fight left the boy in hospital. The incident happened during a heated match.

People who fear spiders should be careful — this might scare you. A man in Wangaratta, in northeast Victoria, was shocked when a large huntsman spider crawled out from inside his car door handle. The video shows him walking up to his black Holden Ute and spraying insect repellent on the door. The spray made the spider come out from under the handle. He calmly says, “Get out, you bastard.” But when the spider’s long, hairy legs suddenly appear, he screams and jumps back in fear.

Tottenham's manager, Mauricio Pochettino, says Harry Kane is like the great striker Gabriel Batistuta. He also says he'll be there to support Kane if he ever has a bad spell. Kane scored just 79 seconds after coming on in his first full England game against Lithuania. That brought him to 29 goals for the season. England's manager, Roy Hodgson, is careful not to expect too much from Kane. Kane has gone up fast since he finally made the Tottenham first team after playing on loan at Leicester and Norwich.. Pochettino says Kane is like Gabriel Batistuta.

A former footballer who ran a £30 million investment scheme and lived like a millionaire is now surviving on handouts, a court has heard. Michael McIndoe played for Bristol City and Wolverhampton Wanderers. He convinced other footballers to join his scheme by promising a 2% return on their money. The scheme failed, and he ended up with over £2 million in debt. He was declared bankrupt in October last year. Once known as 'Mr Big' in Marbella, where he enjoyed parties with glamorous women, he is now being pursued by creditors in court.

Juventus director Pavel Nedved has said Barcelona are interested in signing Paul Pogba. In an interview with Mundo Deportivo, the former Juventus player, who made 324 appearances for the club, said Pogba will not be leaving Juventus. He also said he was happy that Juventus did not face Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals. Nedved, who played for Juventus, confirmed that Pogba is staying at the club.

A man who has a criminal record for sex offenses was reportedly run over by his girlfriend after she said she caught him abusing a 2-year-old girl. James Oliver, 48, suffered a serious leg injury when he was hit by a car driven by Linda Currier, 53. Police found Oliver in the driveway of a house in Noblesboro, Maine, on Saturday night, according to NBC News. Authorities say the couple had an argument inside the home after Currier saw Oliver allegedly trying to sexually harm the young child.

Liverpool's target, goalkeeper Neto, is also wanted by PSG and several clubs in Spain, meaning Brendan Rodgers faces strong competition to sign him, according to Neto’s agent, Stefano Castagna. Liverpool were linked with Neto earlier in the season when Simon Mignolet was dropped. A move in January didn't happen, but Neto is expected to leave Fiorentina in the summer when his contract ends in June. Neto was seen rushing from his goal during Fiorentina’s match against Roma in March, as Juan Iturbe approached.

Not everyone should drive a $50,000 car. That’s the message from a video posted by YouTube user Richard Stewart showing a Porsche Cayman losing control after running a green light in Prince Edward Island, Canada. The sports car swerved sharply and crashed into a concrete barrier. One wheel came off before the car stopped. Stewart wrote on YouTube: "Just because you have a nice car doesn’t mean you’re a good driver. Don’t let your son drive your Porsche!"

Sunderland vs Newcastle United (Stadium of Light)  
Team news:  
Sunderland: Midfielder Lee Cattermole will start in the team for Sunday's derby against Newcastle. Head coach Dick Advocaat confirmed Cattermole is back after serving a two-match ban. He was suspended because he reached the limit of 10 yellow cards for the season.

If Rory McIlroy wins the upcoming Masters, he will complete a career grand slam, marking the end of a lifelong journey for the world’s top golfer. In partnership with his sponsor Bose, McIlroy has released a video showing his path from playing on small courses as a child to becoming a world champion, including some tough moments along the way. The video starts with McIlroy jogging early in the morning, with the words "Six weeks to Georgia" on screen. It also includes an interview with a young Rory McIlroy, before he became a famous golfer.

Sergio Garcia says he is focused on winning his first PGA Tour title since 2012 at this week’s Shell Houston Open. Even though the Masters is coming up soon, and big stories like Rory McIlroy trying to win his third major in a row and whether Tiger Woods will return to golf are getting a lot of attention. Garcia is still only thinking about ending his long winless streak. The course in Houston is set up to feel like Augusta, but he’s staying focused on his own goal. He was putting during the Cadillac Championship in Doral, Florida, last month.

Riki Hughes, a former Iraq war soldier, has been jailed for 16 months after stealing £17,000 from Tidworth Town Football Club, where he volunteered as club secretary. He used the money for personal expenses, including camping gear and a stag trip to Las Vegas. He lied about using the money to pay rent, even though the club was not actually paying rent. The case was heard at Salisbury Crown Court. Hughes, 31, admitted taking the money and was sentenced to prison.

Johnny Sexton has become very used to success. Winning big trophies has become a regular part of his life — something he does every year and is determined to keep doing. As he got ready to play in the European Champions Cup quarter-final against Saracens in Paris, the Racing Metro player and Irish star looked back at his winning ways. He said, “I’ve been lucky to play with great teams at Leinster and Ireland. There haven’t been many years when I wasn’t on a team that won a trophy.” In fact, since he started playing at the senior level, 2010 is the only year he didn’t win a major prize.

Mustafa Kamal stepped down as ICC president on Wednesday. He said India influenced the result of the Cricket World Cup quarter-final between Bangladesh and India. He made the comments at the airport when he returned from the tournament in Australia. Kamal, who is from Bangladesh, said everyone could see what happened in the Bangladesh-India match. He accused India of using its position in the ICC to affect the game's outcome. He also said he would have reacted the same way if any other country had been treated this way. Mustafa Kamal, who is pictured with the Cricket World Cup trophy, is no longer the ICC president.

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce has defended Nigel Pearson and said he respects him for being true to himself. They worked together when Allardyce was at Newcastle in 2007, and they will meet again this Saturday when West Ham play Leicester at the King Power Stadium. Pearson has been in the spotlight for several controversial moments this season, including grabbing Crystal Palace’s James McArthur by the throat and losing his temper with a reporter during a press conference. Leicester’s manager, Nigel Pearson, has been involved in a number of controversial incidents this season.

Skipper John O'Shea is urging Sunderland to win their fifth straight derby against Newcastle. The match takes place on Sunday at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland have won the last four derbies, but they badly need three points to stay clear of the fight to avoid relegation from the Barclays Premier League. If Burnley beat Tottenham earlier in the day, Sunderland could drop into the relegation zone. That makes winning the match essential.

Stoke manager Mark Hughes says it's time to stop losing at Chelsea's stadium. Since Stoke were promoted to the Premier League in 2008, they have played Chelsea away in all competitions eight times and lost every match. Their last win at Stamford Bridge was in 1995, in a League Cup game. Since a 1-1 draw in 1984, Stoke haven’t even drawn a game there. The most recent match was a 3-0 Chelsea win, with Frank Lampard celebrating.

Newcastle are hoping to avoid a third straight loss when they play rivals Sunderland in Sunday’s big derby.. They’ve been struggling lately without their banned striker Papiss Cisse. Although Newcastle are at the bottom of the Premier League, they’re only one point above the teams in the relegation zone. But if it weren’t for Cisse’s goals, they’d actually be two points further down, near the bottom. Cisse is Newcastle’s top scorer this season with 11 goal, and 10 of those have been important in turning games in Newcastle’s favor.

Dick Advocaat is going to bring back Lee Cattermole, who plays as a tough midfielder, to the heart of his Sunderland team. They are trying to avoid being relegated again, and this would be their fifth straight derby win. Cattermole, 27, was banned from playing in the last two games because he got 10 yellow cards this season. That meant he couldn’t play in Advocaat’s first game as manager, a 1-0 loss to West Ham on March 21. But at Friday’s team meeting, Cattermole was told he will start for sure against Newcastle on Sunday. Advocaat wants a strong performance from him, as

For Ronny Deila, qualifying for the Champions League isn’t just about money. But now there are 16 million reasons to get Celtic there — a fourth straight title. And every reason has to do with money. This week, UEFA announced the new money system for the next three years of European football. The last time Celtic played in the Champions League group stage, in 2013-14, they played against AC Milan, Ajax, and Barcelona. They won just one game and earned £12.6 million. If they do as well or better next season, that amount would go up by £4 million. If they get to the last 16, they’ll earn more than £20 million. And that’s without counting ticket sales.

Tottenham defender Ben Davies says he won’t let personal feelings get in the way when he plays against his Wales teammate Sam Vokes at Burnley on Sunday. Spurs are going to Turf Moor hoping to keep their good form going after only one loss—in a match against Manchester United—in their first four Premier League games before the international break. They’re still hoping to qualify for European competition. Burnley are fighting to avoid relegation and are currently 18th in the table, just one point above the danger zone. Sam Vokes, who plays for Burnley, celebrated scoring against Tottenham in the FA Cup earlier this season. That game took place at Turf Moor in the third round, and at the time, Ben Davies turned away after Burnley equalled the score.

Neil Redfearn is thinking about whether he will stay as manager of Leeds United after the club suspended his assistant, Steve Thompson on Thursday. Leeds took two months to hire Thompson. But yesterday morning, Thompson received a letter from director of football Nicola Salerno saying he would be suspended until the end of the season. This means he will not stay at Leeds after just 105 days. He has also been told that the club will not renew his contract when it ends. Leeds United assistant manager Steve Thompson has been suspended by the club.

John Carver says he might use a whip to motivate his Newcastle players before Sunday’s Tyne-Wear derby at the Stadium of Light. The Magpies have lost the last four games against Sunderland. Carver, who was assistant to Alan Pardew during those losses, admits Sunderland played harder in those matches. He said, “In the last four games, Sunderland outworked us – and that’s not good.” He added that he will “whip” his players to make sure they’re ready and motivated to beat Sunderland on Sunday.

David Templeton has strongly criticized the training methods used at Rangers under Ally McCoist and Kenny McDowall. The Ibrox winger said Stuart McCall brought a new style of coaching and tactics that he felt was missing under the old management. Templeton also praised McCall's positive effect since he joined on a short-term deal last month. Rangers have won their last two games, which has boosted team confidence ahead of Saturday’s home match against Hearts, who won the Championship title. Rangers winger David Templeton is very positive about the change Stuart McCall has made since taking charge.

Celta Vigo player Nolito says Lionel Messi should not play in Sunday’s La Liga game. Instead, he says Messi should go to the beach. Nolito joked that he would even call Messi’s dad. Messi has a foot injury but has been training and is expected to be fit. He trained with teammate Javier Mascherano on Thursday.

Robbie Neilson says players like captain Danny Wilson will only leave Hearts if he thinks it’s the right decision for the club.. As Sportsmail reported, Celtic are interested in signing Wilson, a former Rangers defender, and have put him on their list of possible summer signings. Before Sunday’s Championship game against Rangers, Neilson acknowledged that outside interest in his promoted players is normal. But he made clear that he won’t sell any players unless he agrees it’s the right move for Hearts.. He also agrees with owner Ann Budge that any departures must be approved by him, and only if the price is right.

Sam Allardyce has warned Brendan Rodgers that giving Raheem Sterling a big new contract could cause problems with the rest of the Liverpool team. He thinks if Sterling gets paid more than the £ £100000000 a week he was already offered, his teammates might demand higher pay too. Allardyce says he doesn’t blame Sterling, who earns £35,000 a week at Liverpool, for wanting to earn as much as possible. He believes there are very few young players with real talent, so clubs are paying huge wages to get any good ones they can. Raheem Sterling, a Liverpool and England player, has not yet signed a new contract with Liverpool.

Blackpool are talking about signing Austria defender Thomas Piermayr, who is 25 and has been training with the Championship club this week. They want to bring him in, and it is expected he will join for the upcoming season, which will be in League one. Piermayr is a free agent, meaning he is not under contract, and he recently played for Colorado Rapids. He also played for Inverness Caledonian Thistle in 2011. He has not been in England before,, but Blackpool may be to give him his first chance to play there.

Tony Pulis wants to talk to West Bromwich Albion chairman Jeremy Peace after the team is safe from relegation. He believes the club needs big changes to return to the top half of the Premier League. Pulis said the team has been off track in recent years and needs major improvements. West Brom finished 10th and 8th under Roy Hodgson and Steve Clarke, but struggled last season and ended up 17th. Tony Pulis, West Brom's manager, is shown shouting from the sideline during a match against Manchester City.

Arsenal legend Ian Wright is upset that Theo Walcott might leave the club. He thinks Walcott has struggled at Arsenal because Arsene Wenger won't play him as a striker.. Wright says Walcott has only started five times this season since coming back from a serious knee injury that kept him out for seven months. With Arsenal now looking to sign Raheem Sterling and Walcott's contract ending next summer, Wright fears the team could lose a key player..

Roberto Martinez believes Ross Barkley can become an even more important player for Everton and England, after overcoming his second-season struggles at Goodison Park. Barkley has had a mixed season with Everton, following his selection for England’s World Cup squad last summer and a knee injury that delayed his return to action. However, England manager Roy Hodgson has kept him in the team. Martinez is encouraged by Barkley’s two recent substitute appearances for England, against Lithuania and Italy, and thinks he’s now ready to improve again.

England will not play in the Under-19 European Championships this summer after losing 2-1 to France in their final qualifier. The match was in Saint-Lo. England had won their first two games in the Elite Round, against Denmark and Azerbaijan. They needed to beat France to qualify for the finals in Greece in July. France scored through Sehrou Guirassy and Gnaly Cornet, taking the lead. Fulham's Patrick Roberts scored late, but it wasn't enough to get England through.

Newcastle midfielder Jonas Gutierrez is hoping to mark his return to first-team football with a win in the local derby against Sunderland. The 33-year-old Argentinian has been on the bench in each of the last three games since coming back from testicular cancer. and has been warmly welcomed by teammates and fans. But he’s been on the losing side each time. Now, he wants to end that streak as Newcastle try to recover from their worst run of four straight losses to Sunderland. at the Stadium of Light on Sunday.

After a close game between South Sydney and Canterbury at ANZ Stadium in Sydney on Good Friday, NRL referees and officials were hit with plastic water bottles by angry fans. The Rabbitohs won 18-17 in the final minute. The match was controversial because the referees penalised Bulldogs captain James Graham in the last minute, which gave the Rabbitohs the win. As the referees, officials, and players walked off the field after the game, some fans threw bottles and shouted insults at them.

Kevin Sinfield, the former England rugby league captain and legendary Leeds Rhinos leader, has been warned he will be a target when he moves to rugby union. The 34-year-old player announced he will leave rugby league at the end of the season. He will join Yorkshire Carnegie, the sister club of Leeds Rhinos, on an 18-month contract. This move has surprised the rugby league world.

Raheem Sterling says he isn’t ready to sign a new contract with Liverpool, even though he was offered a £100-a-week deal to stay. The 20-year-old winger said in a BBC interview that he would have accepted a much lower pay deal just a year ago. Although he's one of Liverpool's top players, Sterling hasn't played as well this season. He has scored six goals so far this season—just one more than Stoke's Jon Walters. His goal-scoring rate and how often he plays per goal have also gone down, as shown in the chart below.

Brighton and Hove Albion are teaching their young players about the law and ethics of sexual consent. The club is the first in the Championship to offer this kind of training and counselling. The Protect, Inform and Prevent (PIP) programme helps players understand when consent is legally accepted. The training includes private Q&A sessions where players can talk about past experiences. These sessions are led by a former police detective and a psychotherter.

A new video shows homeless people reading mean tweets that were written about them. The video was made by the agency Leo Burnett Toronto for the charity Humans For Humans. It aims to make people think differently about people who sleep on the streets. Many of the people cry while reading messages like, "I hate the homeless, I don’t feel sorry for you," and "I saw a homeless girl across the street. I almost vomited." The video is below.

George Boyd is the hardest-working player in the Barclays Premier League this season, running 210.5 miles during games. That’s as far as running from Burnley’s Turf Moor stadium to Crystal Palace’s Selhurst Park in south London.. He has run a little farther than Tottenham midfielder Christian Eriksen. Normally, walking that distance would take 69 hours, but Boyd covered it in less than 40 hours of game time. George Boyd is the Barclays Premier League's hardest working player, clocking up 210.5 miles on the pitch..

Police have arrested the parents of a five-month-old baby who died yesterday. The baby, from Perry Barr in Birmingham, was taken to Birmingham Children's Hospital after being found unresponsive with breathing problems. The parents, both 5, were arrested after the child died. Police were called to their home just before 1am yesterday morning. The death is being treated as suspicious, and a post mortem will be done today to find out the exact cause.

Raheem Sterling is not being disloyal to Liverpool by delaying talks about a new contract until the summer, says player's chief Gordon Taylor. The 20-year-old England player has been offered a deal believed to be worth £100,000 a week, by manager Brendan Rodgers, who called it "an incredible offer." But no agreement has been reached yet. Sterling says he is not just after money. Taylor, who is also the head of the Professional Footballers' Association, thinks waiting until the end of the season could be a smart move. In a TV interview, Sterling said he is not ready to sign a new contract with Liverpool.

Anderson hasn't done well since leaving Manchester United to go back to Brazil. On Wednesday, his own mistake was overshadowed by a worse error from a teammate. The Brazilian midfielder was sent off in the first half for pushing a player from Ypiranga Erechim, Otacilio Neto, even though the push happened when the ball wasn was in play. The opponent was also sent off for hitting back with an elbow. But Anderson got lucky because his teammate, Fabricio, made a bigger mistake by swearing at their own fans. That led to Fabricio getting a red card too, making Internacional play with only nine players. The game ended in a 1-1 draw in Porto Alegre.

A seven-year-old boy was raped and set on fire by two teenagers after he went to buy food. Police say the boys took him to a remote area and raped him. When he tried to fight back, they set him on fire. The boy, who had burns covering 30% of his body, managed to escape. Inspector Sasthe told PTI about the incident. The attack happened in Padma Nagar, Bhiwandi, a suburb of Mumbai. Police are now investigating the case.

A pug named Dug has made a surprising recovery after being bitten in the face by a rattlesnake.. Dug and his owner, Lindsay Castro were hiking on the Jurupa Hills trail in Fontana, California, on Thursday. They heard a rattling sound, and Lindsay stepped back, but Dug ran toward the snake and got bitten. The bite caused his face to swell instantly to twice its normal size. The incident was captured on video.

Jose Mourinho might one day surprise everyone by returning to manage Real Madrid, even after his difficult departure, says Real Madrid defender Alvaro Arbeloa. Mourinho left Real Madrid after three years to return to Chelsea in 2013. He left under a cloud, with reports of arguments with key players like club captain Iker Casillas, Sergio Ramos, and Pepe. But Arbeloa, who has played in 25 first-team games this season, says Real Madrid will always keep the door open for Mourinho to come back as manager. He adds that Mourinho could still take charge of Real Madrid one day.

Liverpool's hopes of qualifying for the Champions League ended on Saturday at the Emirates. The manager, Brendan Rodgers, admitted in a short press conference that their chances were gone. He didn't hide that it had been a tough season. After coming close to winning the title last year, they have now fallen out of the race. It's a hard blow for a club that was hoping to return to greatness. Rodgers stayed positive, as he always does, but he didn't pretend the season wasn’t difficult. Still, the team seems to be making progress under him.

Inter Milan coach Roberto Mancini was angry after his team drew 1-1 with Parma, who are at the bottom of the league. He cancelled the players' Easter day off and made them train early on Sunday morning. The first team trained at 8 a.m. local time. Club vice-president Javier Zanetti and sporting director Piero Ausilio were at the training session. Mancini was upset with how the players played. The draw left Inter in ninth place, level with Genoa, and 10 points behind the teams that qualify for European football. Mancini made the players train on Easter Sunday.

Most fans want to own a special piece of memorabilia from their favourite player or team.. and small pieces of history can sell for thousands of pounds. But you might be surprised to learn that an old passport belonging to Paul Parker—best known for playing as a right back for Manchester United and England in the 1990s— was listed on eBay for £5,000. The item was posted earlier in March, and bidding ended on Tuesday. But no one knows for sure if anyone actually paid that large amount. Paul Parker, who played for Manchester United and England, once had this passport. It was sold on eBay.

He has been seen in toast, pancakes, crisps, and even ice cream. But a builder was shocked when he found a picture of Jesus Christ on a piece of wood just a few days before Easter. Paddy Morrall saw the full-size image of Jesus on a broken scaffolding board in Inverness, Scotland, on Wednesday. The image appeared after the wood was left out in the rain for several hours. Jesus is shown wearing a robe. Paddy Morrall, a 31-year-old builder from Keighley, near Bradford, has kept the board.

Ondrej Duda scored in the second half to give Slovakia a 1-0 win over the Czech Republic on Tuesday in a friendly match. The 20-year-old midfielder scored with a low shot from outside the penalty area in the 49th minute— his second goal for Slovakia. This was Slovakia’s third win in 10 matches against the Czechs since the split of Czechoslovakia in 1993. The Czechs have won five of the 10 games. Martin Skrtel was shown a yellow card for kicking Daniel Kolar in the face with a high boot during the match. Slovakia players celebrated their 1-0 win, which continues their strong recent performance.

Karim Benzema showed he’s more than just a football player. The Real Madrid star shared a video of himself rapping while driving his Bugatti Veyron. The video came just before Real Madrid’s La Liga game against Granada at the Bernabeu on Sunday. In the clip, Benzema sings along to Tupac’s song 'Check Out Time'. He might have been better off singing 'All Eyez on Me' instead, since he’s still trying to score. So far this season, he hasn’t scored any goals in all competitions — that’s zero goals. Benzema, who plays for Real Madrid and France, is showing off his singing skills in the video.

A wealthy businessman who supports UKIP, Harvey Boulter, is trying to stop a popular Conservative candidate from winning an election. Boulter already gave £ 30,000 to a UKIP candidate running against Liam Fox in Somerset, as part of a long-standing grudge against Fox. He is also spending another £ 30,000 on helping to defeat Tom Tugendhat, the Tory candidate in Tonbridge and West Malling, Kent.

In the last four minutes of the Yorkshire derby between Sheffield Wednesday and Huddersfield, the game ended in a 1-1 draw. Substitute Sergiu Bus scored for Sheffield Wednesday in the 86th minute. Then, substitute Ishmael Miller scored for Huddersfield just before the final whistle to equalize. This result means Huddersfield have not won in their last seven games. They are now 18th in the league, six places and nine points behind Sheffield Wednesday. Sergiu Bus celebrated after scoring the goal that put Sheffield Wednesday ahead.

Stuart Dallas has come a long way since Mark Warburton found him playing part-time on a muddy field for Crusaders in Northern Ireland, for just £70 a week. The 23-year-old scored two brilliant goals as Brentford beat Fulham 4-1 on Good Friday. He had already impressed for Northern Ireland earlier in the week. Brentford now believe they can do more than just reach the play-offs — they’re aiming for Premier League promotion. Three years ago, Warburton spotted Dallas playing in a local game. Dallas celebrated his second goal with joy. This season, he’s been a key player in Brentford’s strong push toward the Premier league.

Baseball is often seen as America's favorite pastime, so it's not surprising that many people feel strongly about their favorite professional team. The New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox are the two most famous and most historic teams. They are the top two teams in popularity, with the Yankees ranked first and the Red Sox second, based on how many people say they are their favorite. The Texas Rangers and Atlanta Braves also have a large number of fans, especially in the southern U States. However, some teams don't have as many fans—like the New York Mets. Scroll down to watch the video.

A high school basketball star has won hearts by asking a girl with Down syndrome to be his prom date............. Trey Moses, a senior at Eastern High School in Louisville, Kentucky, is going to play college basketball for Ball State next year. He asked Ellie Meredith to the prom during her P.E. class. Trey volunteers with teens who have learning disabilities. He surprised her with flowers and a sign that said, "Let's Party Like it's 1989" — a nod to a Taylor Swift album, which is Ellie’s favorite. Ellie said yes and told CNN she’s excited to go dress shopping because she’s already told "a million people" about it.

On April Fools' Day, President Barack Obama joked around by pretending to be the fictional president Frank Underwood from the show *House of Cards*. He wore a fake beard and spoke with a Southern accent, just like the character. In the video, he said, "Hello everybody. This is not Frank Underwood," then added, "This is Barack Obama. Happy April Fools' Day. Frank learned it from me." The character Frank Underwood is played by actor Kevin Spacey, who often speaks in a dramatic, Shakespearean style.

Caykur Rizespor midfielder Ludovic Obraniak was taken to the hospital on Saturday after feeling unwell during a match against Fenerbahce. He was substituted just 30 minutes into the game. Obraniak, a Polish player, was taken for tests because doctors suspected a heart problem. The club said on social media that he was not in immediate danger after initial tests. Obraniak is on loan from Werder B B in Germany. Moussa Sow scored for Fenerbahce, who won the match 5-1.

Three people were taken to hospital after a head-on crash between a vintage 1973 E-Type Jaguar and a Toyota Kluger. The accident happened on Easter Sunday night at a traffic light intersection on Warringah Road in Frenchs Forest, northern Sydney. The Jaguar, believed to be worth over $120,000, was completely destroyed. No one was hurt in the crash, but all three adults were sent to hospital as a safety measure. NSW police are still looking into what caused the crash.

People in Lijin village, in Dongying city, Shandong Province, China, have been seen carrying natural gas in large plastic bags. Some of these bags are as long as six meters. They carry the gas on rickshaws. Pictures show this happening often. The gas is dangerous and can explode if it comes near a flame or cigarette. Because of this, people walking by are worried and say it’s like carrying a bomb. This practice is common in some villages in Shandong. Local news says people do this to save money on gas transport.

Tiger Woods has been seen hitting golf balls on the practice range at Augusta National, which is raising hopes that he might play in this year’s Masters.. He hasn’t played on the PGA Tour since pulling out of the Farmers Insurance Open on February 5 due to a back injury. He has since taken time off to recover and get back in shape. There has been talk he might come back for the Masters, a tournament he has won four times before. He was seen practising at Augusta on Tuesday and is reported to have returned to the course. Tiger Woods has also dropped out of the top 100 in the world rankings for the first time in nearly 19 years.

The BBC has been criticized for spending thousands of pounds of licence fee money on a four-page guide that teaches its staff how to use emojis properly. The guide was created after BBC bosses asked an agency to study how emojis could be used in news stories and on social media. The BBC also paid for special emoji designs of famous people like Gary Lineker and Graham Norton. Even though the BBC spent money on this emoji guide, it later used a sad face emoji to mark the death of the world’s oldest woman.

One of the world’s top long-distance runners and a frequent training partner of Mo Farah says he is scared for his life. After telling Ugandan authorities that a coach has been sexually abusing female runners, some as young as 5. Moses Kipsiro, who won the 10,000m title at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow last year, said five female runners came to him for help. He also said he has received death threats since reporting the abuse to his national sports federation and the police.

Patrick Kluivert, a former Dutch footballer and assistant coach, has started his time as Curacao’s coach with a win in the 2018 World Cup qualifiers. Curacao moved on to the second round of CONCACAF qualifying after a 2-2 draw in Montserrat. They had already won 2-1 in the first leg in Willemstad. The overall result was 4-3 in Curacao’s favor. Kluivert, who once worked with Louis van Gaal at the 2014 World Cup, helped lead Curacao to the next stage.

An 18-year-old college student who was caught on video biting the head off a live hamster has been kicked out of his fraternity,, been removed from college, and is being sent for a mental health evaluation. The student, Brady Eaves, is the stepson of a former Mississippi governor candidate and was privately educated. The video, filmed during a drunken Spring Break party in Florida, shows him laughing as he kills the animal. The video was first reported by DailyMail.com. Authorities could charge Eaves with a felony for animal cruelty, which could result in up to five years in jail and a $5,00 fine.

Sri Lanka's sports minister, Navin Dissanayake, said Kumar Sangakkara should think again about his decision to retire from limited-overs cricket and play for one more year. Sangakkara had retired from one-day cricket on March 18, after losing in the World Cup quarter-final. He said he was sad about the loss but happy that Sri Lanka was in a better position now than when he started in 200.. The minister made this request to reporters on Wednesday, after naming a new temporary group to run cricket, led by former test player Sidath Wettimuny.

Edinburgh have brought back three Scotland internationals — Dougie Fife, Alasdair Dickinson, and Ross Ford — for Sunday's European Challenge Cup quarter-final against London Irish. They had been rested for last week's 26-15 Pro12 win over Scarlets in Llanelli, after playing in the RBS Six Nations. Now, head coach Alan Solomons has recalled them to face London Irish at the Madejski Stadium, aiming to field his strongest team. The match is a key chance for the Scots to prove themselves.

Chris Ramsey says Tony Pulis is one of the best British coaches, but he doesn't think he needs to learn tactics from him. Ramsey’s QPR face West Brom on Saturday at the Hawthorns. QPR are 19th in the Premier League, four points behind Sunderland in 17th. Since the start of the year, QPR have only got four points and need a strong finish like Pulis’s 2013-14 season with Crystal Palace. when they earned 17 points from their last eight games to avoid relegation. Ramsey spoke about Pulis ahead of the important match against West Brom.

An 18-year-old girl, Silhan Ozcelik, has appeared in court. She is accused of planning to go abroad to join Kurdish fighters fighting against the Islamic State. She was last seen in October, when she was 17, after she disappeared from her family home in north London. Court records show she traveled on the Eurostar train with another man to Stuttgart, Germany. That city is where the youth wing of the Kurdish Workers’ Party (PKK) is based. She is also accused of preparing to carry out a terrorist attack in October 2014.

Leicester City midfielder Esteban Cambiasso knows what it's like to win football's biggest trophies, but he says saving Leicester from relegation would be one of the best moments of his career. Cambiasso played for Argentina and won five Serie A titles with Inter Milan, where he also won the Champions League in 2010. He told the BBC on Thursday that avoiding relegation would feel just like winning a trophy. He joined Leicester last summer with no transfer fee and signed a one-year contract at the King Power Stadium.

Crystal Palace manager Alan Pardew says Manchester City still have a chance to win the Barclays Premier League title from Chelsea. Last season, City came from behind to win the title, overtaking Liverpool with one game left. This year, the hatchback turns 50. It might not be as fast as a Ferrari or as fancy as a Rolls Royce, but it's the most popular car in the world. The hatchback was first made to help French farmers carry sheep to market. Now, two out of every three cars sold in the UK are hatchbacks. It’s also very popular in cities like Munich and Mexico City because it’s practical, fuel-efficient, and comfortable to drive. The first hatchback ever made was the Renault 16, which came out in April 1965. The Renault 4, which came before it, was originally designed to help French farmers carry sheep.
